findings.title: Concurrency relies only on unique keys; no product-level lock, unlike order-lock.ts, and the fake DB cannot test it
findings.problem: Postgres runs at READ COMMITTED. Count check, first-free-position and the reorder id-list check are reads outside any lock, so races beyond the unique key slip through: reorder reads 5 ids, a concurrent upload inserts a 6th, reorder's step 'move every photo to position+100' then sweeps the new row too and leaves it at 100+; two uploads at 3 photos fail needlessly with a 409 although only 4 exist; delete's gap closing races with upload at the same slot; delete racing with a variant link to the same photo raises an unhandled FK error (P2003 -> 500). The repo's own pattern is lock first, read locked values, write, in one transaction with LOCKED_TX. The test double serialises every transaction (chain in fake-db.ts) and has no productImage model, so 'two simultaneous uploads' cannot reproduce the race and would pass vacuously.
findings.evidence: server/src/commerce/order-lock.ts:24-31 lockOrder uses `FOR UPDATE`; admin.service.ts:200-217 mutate() runs `$transaction(..., LOCKED_TX)`; server/src/test/fake-db.ts:34-45 `chain.then(...)` serialises transactions; spec L105 'the (productId, position) unique key makes the second fail with 409'.
findings.fix:
In section 2, after the "Order of work" intro, add this paragraph.

"Locking. Every operation that reads or changes a product's photos runs in one `prisma.$transaction(..., LOCKED_TX)` (from `server/src/commerce/order-lock.ts`) and starts by calling a new `lockProduct(tx, productId)` helper, placed next to `lockOrder`. The helper runs `SELECT id FROM \"Product\" WHERE id = ${productId} FOR UPDATE` and returns 404 NOT_FOUND when no row comes back. This covers the upload insert, alt change, reorder, delete, variant link, and the `media:seed` and `media:remove-samples` scripts. The variant link endpoint (`PUT /v1/admin/variants/:sku/image`) first resolves the owning product of the sku, locks that product, and only then reads the image and checks that it belongs to the same product. The photo count, duplicate hash, first free position and the reorder id list are all read after the lock, never before it. Files are written to MinIO before the transaction and deleted after commit (or on rollback), as described below, and are never held inside the lock. The two unique keys stay as a backstop. A P2002 maps to 409, and the handler reads `error.meta.target` to choose between \"Foto ini sudah ada di produk ini.\" (hash key) and \"Foto lain sedang diunggah. Coba lagi.\" (position key)."

In the Upload bullet, replace "Two uploads at once on the same product: the `(productId, position)` unique key makes the second fail with 409 \"Foto lain sedang diunggah. Coba lagi.\" instead of creating a seventh photo." with "Two uploads at once on the same product are serialised by `lockProduct`. The second one sees the true count and either succeeds at the next free position or fails with 409 LIMIT_REACHED when the product already has 6 photos."

In the Reorder bullet, add at the end: "The id list is compared with the photo ids read after `lockProduct`, so a photo added by a concurrent upload makes this reorder fail with 409 and is never swept to position + 100."

In the Delete bullet, add at the end: "A variant link to the same photo that arrives at the same time waits for the lock and then fails with 422 `Foto tidak milik produk ini.` or 404, never with an unhandled foreign-key error."

In Testing, replace the line `Six-photo limit, duplicate photo, two simultaneous uploads (fake database like src/test/fake-db.ts), reorder with a stale list, delete clearing a variant link.` with: "Six-photo limit, duplicate photo, reorder with a stale list, delete clearing a variant link. The concurrency tests (two simultaneous uploads at 5 photos, upload during reorder, delete during variant link, upload during delete at the same slot) must not use `fake-db.ts` as it is, because it serialises every transaction (`chain` in `fake-db.ts`) and would pass without any lock. They use either a test double that runs transactions concurrently and enforces both unique keys and `FOR UPDATE` row locks, or a real Postgres. Each such test is written so that removing the `lockProduct` call makes it fail. Also test that `lockProduct` returns 404 for an unknown product."
findings.verifyReason: Checked. The spec (section 2, "Order of work", L105-107) runs the count, free-position, duplicate and reorder-list reads outside any lock. It relies only on the (productId, position) and (productId, hash) unique keys, and it never mentions LOCKED_TX or a product row lock. The repo's own pattern is the opposite. order-lock.ts:24-31 lockOrder uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, and the file header (L1-6) says to lock first, read the locked values, then write. LOCKED_TX is used in admin.service.ts:217 and order.service.ts:123, 182 and 248. The races described are real at READ COMMITTED. A reorder that reads 5 ids can race a concurrent upload, and its "position + 100" sweep then catches the new row. The unique key also fails an upload with 409 when the count is not actually at the limit. Delete's gap closing can race an upload at the same slot. A delete racing a variant link to the same photo gives an FK error. The test double does serialise transactions: fake-db.ts:12 and 34-44 chain each $transaction onto the previous one. A "two simultaneous uploads" test would therefore pass vacuously with or without a lock. The fix does not reverse any approved owner decision; it adds an implementation detail. Refinement: seed and remove-samples are npm scripts rather than endpoints, so the lock rule should cover them separately. The variant-link endpoint receives a sku, so it must resolve and lock the owning product, and read the image after the lock. File writes to MinIO stay outside the transaction.

findings.title: Position rewrites can hit the unique key mid-statement; gap closing on delete is unspecified
findings.problem: The spec fixes reorder with a +100 offset but says only 'close the gap' for delete. A bulk `UPDATE ... SET position = position - 1 WHERE position > x` (or Prisma updateMany with decrement) can fail on @@unique([productId, position]) because Postgres checks a non-deferrable unique index per row, in physical order. The +100 scheme also leaves positions above 5 visible if any step is skipped, and `Int (0-5)` is not enforced by the database (db push cannot create a CHECK).
findings.evidence: spec L43 `@@unique([productId, position])`, L106 'moves every photo of the product to position + 100', L107 'close the gap in positions'.
findings.fix:
1) Replace L107 "close the gap in positions" with: "closing the gap re-numbers the remaining photos with the same two-step scheme as reorder (first set position = position + 100 for all photos of the product, then write 0..n-1 in their current order), inside the same transaction. Never use a single decrementing UPDATE or updateMany with decrement, because the non-deferrable unique key is checked per row."
2) Append to the `position` row in the Data table (L40): "The 0-5 range is not enforced by the database (db push cannot create a CHECK). The service enforces it: upload runs in the transaction, counts the product's photos, and rejects with 409 when the product already has 6 photos, otherwise inserts at the first free position (always <= 5). The unique key only resolves races between two simultaneous uploads."
3) Add one sentence to the reorder bullet (L106): "The +100 step and the final write are in the same transaction, so no position above 5 is ever visible after commit."
findings.verifyReason: Spec L106 gives reorder the two-step +100 scheme, but L107 only says "close the gap in positions" for delete. A single decrementing UPDATE on a non-deferrable unique index `@@unique([productId, position])` (L40) can fail mid-statement. Postgres checks uniqueness per row in physical order, so a row moving 2 to 1 can collide before the row at 1 has moved to 0. The 0-5 range at L40 is only a comment, and a database CHECK is not created with db push. L105 relies on the unique key to stop a seventh photo, but a seventh photo would take position 6, which does not collide, so it needs an explicit cap check. The finding's "count check under the product lock" refers to a lock the spec does not define, so the fix should not assume one. It should use the transaction and the unique key already in L105.

findings.title: Seed and remove-samples run in a separate process, so the API's in-memory catalogue never sees them
findings.problem: The spec says every change is visible 'within the 15-second catalogue cache'. That 15 s is only the HTTP Cache-Control. The server data is an in-memory snapshot built by CatalogService.refresh(), called at start-up and by refreshAfterWrite() after API writes. `npm run media:seed` and `media:remove-samples` run via `docker compose exec api npm run ...`, a different Node process, so the running API keeps serving the old product list (no photos, or removed samples) until restart or an unrelated order/stock write. Also refreshAfterWrite() logs and swallows a failed refresh, so even API uploads can stay stale with no retry. Rollout step 3 then runs the live checks against stale data.
findings.evidence: server/src/commerce/catalog.service.ts:32-35 onModuleInit loads once; :45-51 refreshAfterWrite swallows errors; :126-131 refresh() is the only rebuild; spec L108 'within the 15-second catalogue cache', L154 'npm run media:seed (inside the API container ...)'.
findings.fix:
Replace L108 with: "After every API image write, CatalogService.refreshAfterWrite() rebuilds the in-memory catalogue snapshot (the 15-second Cache-Control is only the HTTP cache on top). A failed rebuild is logged and not retried until the next write or an api restart; the admin response still succeeds."

Add to section 5 after the media:seed / media:remove-samples bullets: "These commands run in their own Node process, so they cannot refresh the API's in-memory catalogue. After either command the operator must make the running API reload, by restarting the api container (`docker compose restart api`) or, if the owner approves a new endpoint, by calling POST /v1/admin/catalog/reload (staff session with products.media permission, audited, calls CatalogService.reload() and surfaces failure to the caller). Default: restart the api container; no new endpoint."

In Rollout: after step 2 (`docker compose exec api npm run media:seed`) add "2b. `docker compose restart api`, then confirm GET /v1/catalog returns images for seeded products." Add the same restart plus confirm step after any media:remove-samples run, and add a line to LAUNCH_CHECKLIST 'Before launch' item: "run media:remove-samples, restart the api, confirm GET /v1/catalog has no sample images".

Add to Tests: "After media:seed and an API restart (or the reload call), the catalogue response contains images for seeded products; after remove-samples and a restart, it contains none with source sample."
findings.verifyReason: Verified in catalog.service.ts. The catalogue is an in-memory Map built by refresh(). It loads once in onModuleInit and again via refreshAfterWrite(), which logs a failed refresh and swallows the error (lines 45-51). Nothing else calls reload() from outside the API process, and no reload endpoint exists. A seed or remove-samples command run by `docker compose exec api npm run ...` is a separate Node process, so the running API keeps its old snapshot until restart or an unrelated write. Spec L108 ties visibility to a "15-second catalogue cache", which is only the HTTP cache. Rollout step 3 would therefore check stale data. The fix does not reverse any approved owner decision. Two refinements: (1) a new admin reload endpoint adds surface and RBAC/audit work, so the simplest choice that needs no new endpoint is to restart the api container in Rollout; (2) the spec's claim of a retry on the next write is accurate, but a failed rebuild after an image write stays stale until some later write, so the wording should say that rather than imply an automatic retry.

findings.title: media:seed can resurrect samples after remove-samples or after a client emptied a product, and races staff uploads
findings.problem: The rule 'add rows only to products that have no photos yet' cannot tell a never-seeded product from one whose samples were deliberately removed, or whose client deleted every photo. Running media:seed again (the Rollout step, a later redeploy script, or a new colleague) silently puts sample photos back on a launched shop, defeating the launch checklist. The seed also does its check outside any lock, so it can interleave with a staff upload (position 0 conflict, or sample inserted ahead of the client's first photo), and it writes no audit entry although remove-samples does.
findings.evidence: spec L154 'only to products that have no photos yet ... running it twice changes nothing'; L155 'media:remove-samples deletes every sample photo (rows and files) with audit entries'; constraint 7 in CLAUDE.md (every admin mutation audited).
findings.fix: Replace the media:seed sentence at L154 with: "`npm run media:seed` (inside the API container on a server) uploads missing files and adds rows with `source: \"sample\"` and `createdBy: \"seed\"` only to products that have no photos AND no earlier image audit entry (`PRODUCT_IMAGE_ADDED`, `PRODUCT_IMAGE_REMOVED`) for that product, so it never brings samples back after `media:remove-samples` or after a client removed every photo. Each sample it adds writes a `PRODUCT_IMAGE_ADDED` audit entry with actor \"seed\", in the same transaction as the row. If a staff upload takes the position first, the unique key makes the seed insert fail with a conflict; the seed skips that product and logs it. It never changes or removes a client's uploads, and running it twice changes nothing." Replace the remove-samples sentence at L155 so it reads: "...deletes every sample photo (rows and files) with a `PRODUCT_IMAGE_REMOVED` audit entry per photo (actor \"seed-cleanup\")." Add to the tests at L189: "seed, remove-samples, seed again leaves zero photos; seed after a staff upload to an empty product leaves the upload as the only photo."
findings.verifyReason: Part of the finding holds, part does not. HOLDS: spec L154 adds samples to any product with no photos, so it cannot tell a never-seeded product from one that remove-samples or the client emptied. A re-run of media:seed (Rollout step L205 or a later script) would bring samples back on a launched shop. The seed also writes no audit entry, while remove-samples (L155) does, and CLAUDE.md constraint 7 asks for audit on admin mutations. DOES NOT HOLD: the race claim. Spec L105 already guards concurrent inserts with the (productId, position) unique key, so a seed that interleaves with a staff upload fails with a conflict instead of corrupting positions or inserting ahead of the client's first photo. No product lock is needed, and the spec has no lock helper to reuse. The fix is therefore narrower than the reviewer proposed. It needs no new audit code, because remove-samples already writes PRODUCT_IMAGE_REMOVED. It does not reverse any owner decision.

findings.title: Variant-photo link: ownership check is outside the lock and the SetNull cascade can deadlock with order stock locks
findings.section: 1. Data and storage (Variant.imageId) and 2 (PUT variants/:sku/image, Delete)
findings.problem: 'The API also checks that a variant only links to a photo of its own product' is a read-then-write with no lock and no DB constraint (the FK points only to ProductImage.id). A concurrent delete of that photo makes the write fail with an unhandled P2003 (500), and nothing is in place if a later code path forgets the check. Separately, deleting a photo makes Postgres update (SetNull) every linked Variant row in an unspecified order, while order and payment transactions hold Variant row locks in sorted SKU order and then wait for the next; the two can wait on each other and Postgres kills one with a deadlock error (an order failing at checkout). The spec's own non-negotiable is no cycles in the lock order.
findings.evidence: spec L51 'imageId String? ... onDelete: SetNull ... The API also checks'; order-lock.ts:1-5 'lock the order row first, then the stock rows ... in sorted order ... never wait on each other in a cycle'; order-lock.ts:38-39 `ORDER BY sku FOR UPDATE`.
findings.fix:
Add to section 2 (Admin API / write rules), after the Delete bullet at L107:

"Lock order for every image write (upload, reorder, alt change, delete, PUT variants/:sku/image): in one transaction, first `SELECT id FROM "Product" WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE` (this serializes image writes per product), then, only where variants are touched, `SELECT sku FROM "Variant" WHERE "productId" = $1 ORDER BY sku FOR UPDATE` (the same sorted-SKU order as `lockStock` in order-lock.ts). No image code path locks an OrderRecord row, and image code never takes a Variant lock before the Product lock, so no cycle with order or payment transactions is possible.

PUT /v1/admin/variants/:sku/image: under the Product lock, in the same transaction, verify that the photo exists (else 404 NOT_FOUND "Foto tidak ditemukan.") and that ProductImage.productId = Variant.productId (else 422 VALIDATION "Foto tidak milik produk ini."), then update Variant.imageId and write the audit entry. imageId null clears the link. Any P2003 from this write is mapped to 409 CONFLICT "Foto baru saja dihapus. Muat ulang halaman." and never surfaces as 500. The FK on Variant.imageId remains the last line of defence; the application check is not the only guard.

Delete (replace L107 wording): in one transaction take the Product lock, then lock all Variant rows of the product in sku order (FOR UPDATE), then delete the ProductImage row (the SetNull update therefore never waits on a variant in a different order), close the position gap and write the audit entry; then delete the files.

Add to the error table: 'Photo for variant link not found | 404 | NOT_FOUND | Foto tidak ditemukan.' and 'Photo deleted during variant link (P2003) | 409 | CONFLICT | Foto baru saja dihapus. Muat ulang halaman.'

Tests to add: (1) PUT with a photo from another product gives 422; (2) PUT with a nonexistent photo id gives 404; (3) a simulated P2003 from the update gives 409, not 500; (4) concurrent photo delete and variant link on the same product ends with either a clean 200 followed by a null link, or a 404/409, with no 500; (5) concurrent photo delete and an order transaction locking the same variants complete without a deadlock error."
findings.verifyReason: Spec L51 states the ownership check in prose only, with no lock or DB constraint. L107 deletes the photo in one transaction and relies on SetNull, and no section says how concurrent delete and link are serialized or how P2003 is mapped. The 422 row at L171 covers only the ownership mismatch. order-lock.ts:39 locks Variant rows with ORDER BY sku FOR UPDATE, after locking the order row, to avoid cycles. The implicit SetNull update on Variant rows follows heap order, so it can wait on a variant in the opposite order from an order transaction and deadlock (Postgres aborts one, so a checkout fails). The risk is low-probability and needs two variants linked to the same photo, but it is real. The reviewer's fix mentions a "product lock", which does not exist in the code today (only OrderRecord, Variant and OrderSequence use FOR UPDATE), so the fix must say to lock the Product row and must not imply an existing mechanism. This does not reverse any owner decision.

findings.title: prisma db push on start is additive today but rolling the API image back will crash-loop it
findings.section: 1. Data and storage and Rollout on dev
findings.problem: Creating ProductImage and a nullable Variant.imageId with FK is safe on the existing database (new empty table, nullable column; Int[] and the cycle Product->ProductImage->Variant are valid on PostgreSQL). But the container CMD runs `prisma db push --skip-generate` without --accept-data-loss. After photos exist, an older image (rollback) tries to drop the ProductImage table and Variant.imageId column; Prisma refuses data-loss changes non-interactively, exits non-zero and `&&` stops node, so the API never starts. The Rollout section only says to back up and has no rollback or abort path. The schema text also omits the inverse relation fields Prisma requires.
findings.evidence: server/Dockerfile:22 `CMD ["sh", "-c", "npx prisma db push --skip-generate && node dist/main.js"]`; server/prisma/schema.prisma:30-58 Product and Variant have no images/imageId; spec L204 'Deploy as before (back up, upload source, rebuild ...)'.
findings.fix:
Rollout on dev, replace step 1 with: "1. Take the database backup first, before the first start of the new image, then deploy as before (upload source, rebuild `api` and `web`); run `nginx -t` on the compose network before restarting. This change is roll-forward only: `db push` adds the table and column without data loss, but once photos exist an older image would try to drop them, `db push` refuses without `--accept-data-loss`, and the API does not start. Rollback means restoring the pre-deploy database backup together with the old image, or keeping the new image and hiding the feature. Do not add `--accept-data-loss` to the container command."

Data and storage, append after the Variant paragraph (L51): "Prisma needs both sides of each relation: `Product` gains `images ProductImage[]` and `ProductImage` gains `variants Variant[]`. `Variant.imageId` is indexed (`@@index([imageId])`)."
findings.verifyReason: server/Dockerfile:22 runs `npx prisma db push --skip-generate && node dist/main.js` without --accept-data-loss. Once ProductImage rows and Variant.imageId values exist, an older image would try to drop that table and column. Prisma refuses that non-interactively, exits non-zero, and `&&` stops node, so the API crash-loops. The Rollout section (spec L202-206) has no rollback or abort path and does not say to back up before the first start. The Data section (L34-51) does not mention the inverse relation fields Prisma requires (Product.images, ProductImage.variants). The fix reverses no approved owner decision.

findings.title: nginx 413 for files over 11 MB is HTML; api() JSON.parse then throws, so the promised 'TOO_LARGE' message never shows
findings.problem: The spec sets client_max_body_size 11m on all of location /v1/. Any upload above 11 MB (the Multer limit is 10 MB) is rejected by nginx itself with an HTML 413 page, before the API runs. The web client's api() calls JSON.parse on every non-empty body, so it throws a SyntaxError instead of an ApiError. The error table promises 413 TOO_LARGE 'Ukuran file maksimal 10 MB.' but that body only comes from the API for files between 10 and 11 MB. Also, 11m applies to every /v1/ route (sign-in, cart price), not only the one upload route.
findings.evidence: web/src/services/http/client.ts:24 `const json = text ? JSON.parse(text) as {...} : {};` ; spec section 3: "`client_max_body_size 11m;` on `location /v1/`"; spec Error messages: "Over 10 MB | 413 | TOO_LARGE"
findings.fix:
Section 3: replace the client_max_body_size bullet with: "`client_max_body_size 11m;` is set only on a dedicated `location ~ ^/v1/admin/products/[^/]+/images$` block. That block repeats the proxy lines of `/v1/` (`proxy_pass http://api:8080;`, `proxy_http_version 1.1;`, `proxy_set_header Host $host;`, `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;`) and sets `error_page 413 = @too_large;`. All other `/v1/` routes keep nginx's 1 MB default. A named location returns the JSON error: `location @too_large { default_type application/json; return 413 '{\"error\":{\"code\":\"TOO_LARGE\",\"message\":\"Ukuran file maksimal 10 MB.\",\"details\":[]}}'; }`. The 11 MB limit leaves room for multipart overhead on a 10 MB file; the Multer 10 MB limit still produces the same TOO_LARGE body for files between 10 and 11 MB."

Section 4, client.ts bullet: add "`api()` parses the response body inside try/catch. A body that is not JSON becomes `ApiError('HTTP', response.statusText)` instead of throwing a SyntaxError. The photo manager also checks `file.size > 10 * 1024 * 1024` in the browser before sending and shows 'Ukuran file maksimal 10 MB.' under the upload area."

Testing section: add "A 12 MB upload on dev returns the JSON `TOO_LARGE` body, not an HTML page. A non-JSON error body in `api()` yields an `ApiError`, not a SyntaxError (unit test)."
findings.verifyReason: Checked the spec and the code. Spec section 3 sets client_max_body_size 11m on all of location /v1/, and nginx answers any larger body with its own HTML 413 page. web/src/services/http/client.ts line 24 runs JSON.parse on every non-empty body with no try/catch, so an HTML 413 throws a SyntaxError and the TOO_LARGE message in the spec's error table is never shown. That message only reaches the user for files between 10 and 11 MB. The 11m limit also applies to every other /v1 route, which the current web/nginx.conf serves as one plain proxy block. The upload route is POST /v1/admin/products/:id/images (spec line 81), so the narrower regex location in the proposed fix matches it.

findings.title: proxy_intercept_errors alone does not turn MinIO's 403 into a 404; the 'GET /media/ answers 404' check would fail
findings.problem: proxy_intercept_errors on only lets nginx hand upstream status codes of 300 and above to error_page. Without an error_page line for 403, MinIO's AccessDenied XML (with its Server and x-amz headers) is passed to the client unchanged. The spec names the directive but gives no error_page, so an implementer following it literally ships MinIO's 403 XML for /media/ and /media/products/, and the spec's own dev check ('answer 404') fails. Related: limit_except returns nginx's own 403 for POST/PUT, not 405.
findings.evidence: spec section 3: "turns MinIO's 403 into a plain 404 (`proxy_intercept_errors`)"; Testing: "`GET /media/` and `GET /media/products/` answer 404 (no listing)"
findings.fix: Replace the last clause of the `/media/` bullet in section 3 with: "Inside `location /media/`: `proxy_intercept_errors on; error_page 403 404 = @media_404;`, `proxy_hide_header` for the `x-amz-*` headers and `Server`, and `limit_except GET { deny all; }` (HEAD is implied by GET). The `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` header is added without `always`, so it applies to 200 and 206 responses only. At server level: `location @media_404 { internal; default_type text/plain; add_header Cache-Control \"no-store\" always; add_header X-Content-Type-Options \"nosniff\" always; return 404 \"Not found\"; }`. MinIO's 403 AccessDenied (listing, or a missing object on a private bucket) and its 404 both become this plain 404 with no MinIO XML or headers. Other methods get nginx's own 403 from `limit_except`, which the same `error_page` also maps to 404; this is intended, so the route reveals nothing." Also add a Testing line: "`POST /media/products/x.webp` answers 404 with no `x-amz-*` or `Server: MinIO` header, and a 404 from `/media/` carries `Cache-Control: no-store` rather than `immutable`."
findings.verifyReason: Spec section 3 (line 116) says the 403 becomes a plain 404 via `proxy_intercept_errors` and names no `error_page`. In nginx that directive only lets `error_page` handle upstream responses with status 300 or above. With no matching `error_page`, MinIO's AccessDenied XML goes to the client unchanged. The Testing line 196 check (`GET /media/` and `/media/products/` answer 404) would then fail wherever MinIO returns 403, and the spec as written would not deliver the 404 it promises. I read the spec only. web/nginx.conf has no `/media/` block yet, so no existing config contradicts the finding. The second point also holds: the spec says "refuses other methods" without a status, and `limit_except ... deny all` returns nginx's own 403, not 405. That is acceptable if the same `error_page` maps it to 404. The reviewer's fix is sound. I tightened it so `add_header` on the 200 response does not leak `immutable` onto errors (no `always` there), and so the existing `proxy_hide_header` of `x-amz-*` stays in force.

findings.title: MINIO_BUCKET cannot reach the web container the way the spec implies without leaking MinIO credentials or silently being empty
findings.problem: MINIO_BUCKET lives in server/.env. Compose `environment: MINIO_BUCKET: ${MINIO_BUCKET}` interpolates from the project-root .env or the shell, not server/.env, so it would be empty or unset. The obvious workaround, `env_file: ./server/.env` on the web service, hands MINIO_SECRET_KEY, the database URL and the signing secrets to a public-facing nginx container (violates least privilege). If the variable is absent, envsubst leaves the literal `${MINIO_BUCKET}`, which nginx then reads as an unknown variable and refuses to start: the whole shop goes down on deploy, and the web image build never runs nginx -t.
findings.evidence: docker-compose.yml:11-17 (web service has no env_file or environment); server/.env.example:7 `MINIO_BUCKET=tian-media`; web/Dockerfile:11 `COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf`; spec: "passes `MINIO_BUCKET` to it"
findings.fix:
In section 3 (spec line 114), replace "and passes `MINIO_BUCKET` to it" with: "and sets only `environment: [\"MINIO_BUCKET=${MINIO_BUCKET:-tian-media}\", \"NGINX_ENVSUBST_FILTER=^MINIO_BUCKET$\"]` on the web service. Never use `env_file: ./server/.env` on web: the web container must not receive MinIO keys, the database URL or signing secrets. Compose reads `${MINIO_BUCKET}` from the root `.env` or the shell, not from `server/.env`, so the root `.env.example` documents `MINIO_BUCKET` and its value must equal the one in `server/.env`. `web/Dockerfile` changes its COPY line to `COPY nginx.conf /etc/nginx/templates/default.conf.template`."

In line 115, append: "The filter limits envsubst to `MINIO_BUCKET`, so any other `${...}` in the template stays literal."

Add to Rollout step 1: "After rebuilding, `docker compose exec web nginx -t` passes, and `docker compose exec web grep -n proxy_pass /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` shows the real bucket name (for example `.../tian-media/media/`), with no `${...}` and no `//media/`. If either check fails, do not restart traffic onto the new web image."
findings.verifyReason: Checked the spec and the repo files. The web service in docker-compose.yml has no env_file or environment. Compose interpolates `${VAR}` from the root .env or the shell, not from server/.env, so `MINIO_BUCKET` would be empty or unset. An unset variable gives a literal `${MINIO_BUCKET}` in the rendered config (envsubst only replaces variables defined in the container), and nginx fails to start on an unknown variable. An empty value gives `//media/`, a silent break. Using `env_file: ./server/.env` would hand MinIO keys to the public nginx container. web/Dockerfile line 11 still copies the config to conf.d, and spec line 115 assumes the templates path, so the Dockerfile change is needed. Spec line 114 says only "passes MINIO_BUCKET to it", which is vague. Rollout step 1 (line 204) already runs `nginx -t`, but it does not check that the rendered config holds the real bucket name. The fix is a spec clarification, not a reversal of an owner decision.

findings.title: srcset widths are chosen by image width, but the square object-fit:cover frame is limited by image height, so landscape photos render soft; width/height attributes are also unsafe
findings.problem: Copies are cut at 480/960/1600 px wide and the photo is not cropped. The frame is square with object-fit: cover, so a 16:9 or 4:3 photo is scaled until its height fills the frame and the browser picks a width candidate for the slot width. Example: a 16:9 photo on a 390 px phone at DPR 3 needs 1170 px of height, but the browser picks 1600w, which is only 900 px high, so it is upscaled about 1.3x. A 480w copy of 16:9 is 270 px high for a ~180 px (x2 = 360 px) card slot, so it is upscaled by about 1.3x. The claim 'the 480 px minimum keeps that crop sharp' checks only the source, not the served copy. Also width/height are set to the largest copy's size (non-square); Tailwind's preflight sets img height:auto, so without explicit classes a non-square image would break the square frame, and the no-layout-shift goal depends on the frame, not on those attributes.
findings.evidence: spec section 2: "The photo is not cropped. Square frames crop it on screen with `object-fit: cover`, and the 480 px minimum keeps that crop sharp."; spec section 3: "Every `` has `srcset` and `sizes`, `width` and `height`"; web/src/components/ui.tsx:31 `aspect-square w-full ... style={{ background: bg }}`
findings.fix: Section 2 "Processing", replace the bullet starting "`rotate()` to apply the orientation tag..." with: "`rotate()` to apply the orientation tag. Widths are measured on the shorter side, because every frame on the storefront and in the admin is square and `object-fit: cover` is limited by the shorter side. For each target in 480, 960 and 1600 that is not larger than the photo's shorter side, make a WebP copy at quality 80 whose shorter side equals the target (resize by width when the photo is portrait or square, by height when it is landscape; the longer side keeps the aspect ratio and is never cropped; no enlargement). When the photo's shorter side is under 1600 px, that shorter side becomes the largest target (for example a shorter side of 1200 gives 480, 960, 1200). Example: a 3000x2000 photo gives 720x480, 1440x960 and 2400x1600 copies. File names, the `sizes` column and the srcset descriptors all use the target (shorter-side) value, not the pixel width of the copy. `width` and `height` store the real pixel size of the largest copy." Replace the bullet "The photo is not cropped. Square frames crop it on screen..." with: "The photo is not cropped. Square frames crop it on screen with `object-fit: cover`. Because the shorter side is what fills the square, copies are measured on the shorter side, and the 480 px minimum guarantees the smallest copy covers a 480 px frame without enlargement." Section 1, `srcset` note, add: "Each `srcset` descriptor `Nw` is the shorter-side target N, which is also the number in the file name, even when the copy's real width is larger (landscape). This is deliberate: the browser then picks the copy by the square frame's size." Section 3, replace "Every `` has `srcset` and `sizes`, `width` and `height`, and `decoding=\"async\"`" with: "Every `` has `srcset` and `sizes`, `width` and `height` (the largest copy's real pixel size, only to give the browser the intrinsic ratio), and `decoding=\"async\"`." Section 4 `ProductPhoto`, add: "The `` has `className=\"absolute inset-0 h-full w-full object-cover\"` (or `h-full w-full object-cover` inside the frame) within the existing `aspect-square` frame, so `width`/`height` never change the frame size and Tailwind preflight's `height:auto` cannot break the square. The frame, not the attributes, prevents layout shift." Testing, replace the "Widths" bullet with: "Widths: a 3000x2000 photo gives 720x480, 1440x960 and 2400x1600 (targets 480/960/1600 on the shorter side); a 2000x3000 photo gives 480x720, 960x1440 and 1600x2400; a photo whose shorter side is 1200 gives targets 480/960/1200; nothing is enlarged. Keys and `sizes` use the shorter-side target; every copy's shorter side equals its target. Keys are built from the hash." Add to the web unit tests: "`ProductPhoto` img has the fill-and-cover classes and the srcset descriptors equal the stored shorter-side targets."
findings.verifyReason: The problem is real. Spec section 2 sizes copies by width (480/960/1600) and does not crop, and ui.tsx:21 shows ProductArt uses a square `aspect-square w-full` frame. ProductPhoto is specified as using that same frame with `object-fit: cover`. Cover scales a landscape photo until its height fills the frame, so the usable resolution is the image height, not its width. A 16:9 photo has a 1600w copy only 900 px high. A 390 px slot at DPR 3 needs 1170 px, so it is upscaled about 1.3x and looks soft. The spec's claim that the 480 px minimum keeps the crop sharp only holds for the source file, not for the served copies. Portrait photos are not affected. The second point is also real but minor. Section 3 requires `width` and `height` attributes, and section 4 never says the img fills the frame, so a non-square img could break the square frame under Tailwind's `height:auto`. No approved owner decision is reversed. The handoff keeps the nominal 480/960/1600 widths and the square frames, and this fix only changes which side those widths are measured on. The reviewer's proposed fix still leaves landscape photos soft, though. If srcset `w` descriptors equal the real pixel width (shorter side x aspect ratio), a 3000x2000 photo's 1440w copy is only 960 px high. A 1170 px slot would then pick 1440w and upscale it by about 1.2x. The descriptor has to be the shorter-side value, so the browser picks by frame height. The browser uses the descriptor only for choosing a candidate, and CSS sets the rendered size, so a descriptor that differs from the pixel width is harmless.

findings.title: Admin photo manager has no persistent place for errors from alt save, reorder, delete or variant link
findings.problem: The spec puts errors only 'right under the upload area' with role=alert. Save-on-blur alt failures (422 empty/too long, 503, 409), reorder 409 ('Muat ulang halaman'), delete failures and variant-link failures happen far from the upload area, possibly off-screen at 375 px. The only other channel is the shared Toaster, which auto-dismisses after 5 s and is a single slot (a later toast replaces an earlier one), so an error can vanish unseen or be overwritten by 'Tersimpan'. Alt text left invalid after a failed blur looks saved.
findings.evidence: Spec: 'Errors appear right under the upload area with role="alert"; successes use the existing toast.' web/src/components/ui.tsx:81 `setTimeout(dismiss, 5000)`; web/src/store/shop.ts:208 `notify` sets one `toast` (replaces previous).
findings.fix: In section 4, Admin, replace the line "Errors appear right under the upload area with `role="alert"`; successes use the existing toast." with: "Each photo row has its own inline error line (`role="alert"`, linked to the field with `aria-describedby`, shown until the next successful action on that row) for alt text, order, main-photo and delete failures; each variant select has the same. The upload area keeps its own error line (`role="alert"`) for upload failures. A failed alt save keeps the typed text, sets `aria-invalid="true"`, and does not show "Tersimpan". Error messages come from the Error messages table. Error toasts are not used for these failures; the toast is only for success. Empty state: "Belum ada foto. Foto pertama yang diunggah menjadi foto utama.""
findings.verifyReason: The spec (line 144) puts errors only under the upload area and uses the shared toast for success. The error table lists failures that occur away from the upload area: alt text 422, reorder 409, variant-link 422, and 503 on any action. The toast is one slot (shop.ts:208 replaces the previous toast) and auto-dismisses after 5 s (ui.tsx:81). So these errors can go unseen, be overwritten by a success toast, or leave a bad alt value that looks saved. No owner decision is reversed. The reviewer's fix also drops error toasts. Keeping the existing error toast tone as a secondary channel is harmless, but inline-only is consistent with the spec.

findings.title: Save-on-blur alt text can be lost or saved silently when navigating away, and 'Tersimpan' is not announced
findings.problem: Alt is saved on blur. Clicking 'Hapus', an up/down button, 'Jadikan utama', or a router link while the field is dirty fires blur and a request while the row is re-ordered or removed; closing the tab or route change mid-request loses the edit with no warning. Reorder or set-main sends a full-order request while an alt PATCH is in flight, with no rule for sequencing. 'Tersimpan' has no stated live-region behavior, so screen reader users get no confirmation; the visual-only confirmation also disappears or never defines its duration.
findings.evidence: Spec: '"Teks alternatif" input ... saved when the field loses focus and confirmed with "Tersimpan"'. Toaster (ui.tsx:85) is `role="status" aria-live="polite"`, but the spec does not say 'Tersimpan' uses it.
findings.fix: Replace the end of the photo-row bullet ("saved when the field loses focus and confirmed with \"Tersimpan\"") with: "saved when the field loses focus, only if the trimmed value changed and is valid (1-125 characters); an empty value is not sent and the default \"Foto {nama produk}\" is shown. Requests for one product (alt, order, set-main, delete) run one at a time in the order issued, so an alt save and a full-order request never overlap. While a row has a request in flight, its field and buttons are `aria-disabled` and show no focus loss side effects. \"Tersimpan\" (or the error message \"Gagal menyimpan. Coba lagi.\" with a retry button) is rendered next to the field inside a `role=\"status\"` (`aria-live=\"polite\"`) region, the same pattern as the Toaster in ui.tsx, and stays visible for at least 5 s or until the next edit. If a row has an unsaved or failed alt, leaving the page (tab close via `beforeunload`, or an in-app link) asks \"Ada teks alternatif yang belum tersimpan.\" Clicking \"Hapus\", an up/down button or \"Jadikan utama\" first waits for the pending alt save to finish, then runs."
findings.verifyReason: Spec line 141 only says the alt field is "saved when the field loses focus and confirmed with Tersimpan". A grep of the spec for aria-live, role=status, beforeunload, queue, in flight and disabled finds nothing relevant. Only line 140 mentions a disabled upload button. So there is no rule for sequencing alt PATCH against reorder, set-main or delete requests, no live-region behaviour or duration for "Tersimpan", and no handling of a dirty or failed alt when the user leaves the page. Blur does fire before a click on a button, so the overlap is real. This does not reverse any owner decision: the handoff "Item 1 decisions" fix alt text as required with a default and say nothing about save timing. The reviewer's fix is somewhat heavy. A per-product request queue and a router prompt add scope, and the 3 s duration is arbitrary. A smaller fix gives the same guarantees.

findings.title: Focus handling after reorder, main-photo and delete is unspecified and the existing Dialog loses focus when the opener is removed
findings.problem: Keyboard reordering is the only reorder method, but nothing says where focus goes after a move. The ↑ on the first row and ↓ on the last are presumably disabled, so pressing ↑ until the photo reaches the top focuses a button that becomes disabled and focus drops to body. Dialog returns focus to the opener on close; after deleting a photo the opener ('Hapus' in the removed row) no longer exists, so `opener?.focus?.()` is a no-op and focus falls to body. No live announcement of the new position is specified.
findings.evidence: web/src/components/Dialog.tsx:31 `opener?.focus?.();` (restores to opener only); spec: '↑ and ↓ buttons; "Jadikan utama"; "Hapus" with the existing `Dialog`' and no focus or announcement rule. Rows must also be keyed by image id for focus to survive the re-render.
findings.fix: Append to the "One row per photo" bullet in section 4: "Rows are keyed by photo id so focus survives re-render. Use `aria-disabled="true"` (not `disabled`) on ↑ for the first row and ↓ for the last row, and ignore the click. After ↑/↓, focus stays on the same button of the moved row. After "Jadikan utama", focus stays on that row's "Jadikan utama" button (now on the first row). A visually hidden polite live region (`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`) announces the result: "Foto 3 dipindah ke urutan 2 dari 4", "Foto dijadikan utama", and after delete "Foto dihapus. 3 foto tersisa". The delete Dialog title names the photo (its alt text and position, e.g. 'Hapus foto 2 dari 4: {alt}?') and puts `autoFocus` on \"Batal\". Because the opener ('Hapus') is removed on confirm, after the Dialog closes (run after Dialog's own focus restore, e.g. in a post-close effect) focus moves to the next row's \"Hapus\" button, or the previous row's if the deleted one was last, or to the upload area's \"Pilih file\" button when no photos remain. If delete is cancelled, Dialog returns focus to that row's \"Hapus\" as it does today." Add a web unit test for focus after move, set-main and delete.
findings.verifyReason: The spec (line 141) lists the row controls and a Dialog for delete but has no focus or live-announcement rule; "toast" is mentioned only for successes. Dialog.tsx line 31 restores focus only to the captured opener (`opener?.focus?.()`). After a confirmed delete the opener's row is gone, so focus drops to body. Disabled end-of-list buttons (↑ on first, ↓ on last) also drop focus if `disabled` is used. Not an owner-decision reversal. The existing toast may not be a live region, so the explicit live region is a reasonable addition. Minor refinement: the Dialog autofocuses `[autofocus]` else the first focusable, so "Batal" default focus needs an `autoFocus` on Batal. Wherever the removed row's Hapus is reused, explicit focus after close must run after Dialog's cleanup (e.g. in a post-close effect or rAF) or it will be overridden.

findings.title: No storage seam defined: MinIO cannot be faked and ObjectStorage has no put-binary, delete or policy methods
findings.section: 1. Data and storage / Testing / Error messages (STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE)
findings.problem: Several required tests depend on controlling storage: files deleted when the insert transaction fails, files deleted after row delete, a failed file delete leaving only an orphan, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE 503 when MinIO is unreachable, bucket policy set at start-up, idempotent media:seed. The existing ObjectStorage only has putText/getText/ensureBucket and constructs an S3Client in its constructor, with no interface to substitute. The 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE row and the bucket policy have no listed test, and the filter has no mapping for S3 errors (they would surface as 500).
findings.evidence: server/src/storage.service.ts:5-52 methods 'ensureBucket', 'putText', 'getText' only; S3Client created in constructor. Spec Error messages row 'MinIO unreachable | 503 | STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE'; Testing section has no storage-failure test.
findings.fix:
Add to section 2 after "Order of work": "Storage seam. Media code reaches the bucket only through an ObjectStorage interface with putObject(key, buffer, contentType), deleteObjects(keys), putBucketPolicy(json) and exists(key), in addition to the existing ensureBucket, putText and getText. The real class wraps the S3 client. Tests inject an in-memory Map implementation with switches to fail the Nth put, any call, or deleteObjects only. Any storage exception during upload, delete, seed or start-up policy is converted to HTTP 503 with code STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, by a wrapper in the media service or a mapping in ApiExceptionFilter for S3 service errors and connection errors, so it never surfaces as 500. A failure to set the bucket policy at start-up is logged and does not stop the API from starting."

Add to Testing, Server unit tests: "Storage failures, using the in-memory storage: (a) the 2nd of 3 puts fails, so the response is 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, no row exists and no files remain; (b) the transaction fails after the puts, so all 3 files are deleted and the original error is returned; (c) deleteObjects fails after the row delete, so the request still succeeds, the row is gone and only unlinked files remain; (d) the policy JSON passed to putBucketPolicy allows only s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::{bucket}/media/* and nothing else, and is applied at start-up; (e) media:seed run twice uploads and inserts nothing the second time, using the in-memory storage; (f) a mapping test that an S3 or connection error yields 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE with the Bahasa Indonesia message from the Error messages table."
findings.verifyReason: Checked the code and spec. server/src/storage.service.ts has only ensureBucket, putText and getText. It builds an S3Client in its constructor and has no interface to substitute. There is no putObject for binary data, no delete and no bucket policy method. The spec requires tests for storage failure paths: files deleted when the insert transaction fails, a failed file delete after the row delete, the 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE row, the start-up bucket policy and an idempotent media:seed. The spec lists none of these tests and defines no way to fake storage; its only fake is the database fake. The string STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE appears only in the spec, not in server/src, and ApiExceptionFilter has no S3 mapping. S3 errors would therefore surface as 500, contradicting the Error messages row. The fix does not reverse any owner decision. It is a testability and wiring detail inside the approved design. Refinements: the policy should also be tested at start-up, where failure should log and not crash the API, and the filter or a wrapper must do the mapping explicitly.

findings.title: Error-table rows map to codes the existing filter and multer cannot produce; several rows have no test, including multipart-level ones
findings.problem: ApiExceptionFilter gives code VALIDATION to any HttpException whose body lacks a 'code' field, so a multer LIMIT_FILE_SIZE (Nest turns it into PayloadTooLargeException with a string body) would return 413 with code VALIDATION, not TOO_LARGE; 415 would also be VALIDATION unless the exceptions are built with a code. Rows with no listed test: 413 TOO_LARGE (and the boundary: exactly 10 MB vs 10 MB + 1 byte), 415 HEIC message distinct from the generic one, Variant links to another product's photo 422, 503, 403 per endpoint body text with {peran}. There is no multipart test harness: package.json has no supertest or @nestjs/testing, existing tests call services directly, and neither sharp nor multer (nor @types/multer) is in package.json.
findings.evidence: server/src/api-exception.filter.ts:26-27 'code: status === 404 ? "NOT_FOUND" : "VALIDATION"' for HttpExceptions without a code; server/package.json devDependencies list only @types/node, prisma, typescript, vitest. Spec row 'Over 10 MB | 413 | TOO_LARGE'.
findings.fix:
1) In section 2, after the "Checks on upload" list, add: "Error codes. `ApiExceptionFilter` gives code VALIDATION to any HttpException whose body has no `code`, and Nest turns multer's LIMIT_FILE_SIZE into a plain 413. So every failure in the Error messages table is thrown as an HttpException whose body is `{ code, message }` (for example `new HttpException({ code: 'UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA', message }, 415)`). The multer LIMIT_FILE_SIZE error is caught in the media controller (or a small exception filter on that route) and rethrown as a 413 with `{ code: 'TOO_LARGE', message: 'Ukuran file maksimal 10 MB.' }`. The existing filter stays unchanged. Add a filter test for this conversion."

2) In section 2 or Dependencies, add: "New dependencies, exact versions pinned like the rest of `server/package.json`: `sharp` and `multer` in dependencies, `@types/multer` in devDependencies. `@nestjs/platform-express` already provides the multer integration."

3) In Testing, replace the first two server bullets (type detection and size limits) with: "Table-driven test, one case per row of the Error messages table, asserting HTTP status, `error.code` and the exact Bahasa message through `ApiExceptionFilter`. It includes: JPEG, PNG and WebP accepted; SVG, GIF and a renamed .txt give the generic 415 message; a HEIC fixture (ftyp heic header bytes; sharp may report format `heif`) gives the HEIC message; a file of exactly 10 MB is accepted and 10 MB + 1 byte gives 413 TOO_LARGE; 479 px and 480 px short side; 40 MP and over; alt text of 0, 1, 125 and 126 characters; a variant linked to another product's photo gives 422; storage failure (fake MinIO client that throws) gives 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE; each of operations and cs gets 403 with the role name in `{peran}`."

4) In Testing add: "Harness: controller-level tests call the controller method with a hand-built `Express.Multer.File` (buffer, mimetype, size), the same way existing tests call services directly. Multipart parsing and the real multer limit are checked once by the dev-server run (upload an over-limit file and a normal file through nginx and the API). No supertest or @nestjs/testing dependency is added."
findings.verifyReason: Checked the spec and the filter code. api-exception.filter.ts lines 22-31 only keep a code when the HttpException body has a `code` field. Otherwise they return 404 as NOT_FOUND and everything else as VALIDATION. Nest turns multer's LIMIT_FILE_SIZE into a PayloadTooLargeException with a plain message body, so as written it would return 413 with code VALIDATION, not TOO_LARGE. A 415 raised without a code would behave the same way. The spec says "Each failure returns the standard body" (line 87) but never says how the new codes (UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA, TOO_LARGE, LIMIT_REACHED, STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE, CONFLICT, FORBIDDEN) are produced. Testing (lines 179-191) has no per-row check of status, code and message. Only "refused with the right code" and "size limits" are listed. It has no test for the exact 10 MB boundary, the HEIC message versus the generic one, a variant linked to another product's photo (422), 503, or the 403 text with {peran}. server/package.json has vitest only. It has no supertest or @nestjs/testing, and the spec never lists multer or @types/multer as additions (sharp is named, but only as a pinned version). No approved owner decision in the handoff "Item 1 decisions" is reversed: the 10 MB limit, the formats and the approach are unchanged, and the fix only adds test and error-mapping detail. The reviewer's fix is sound. I trimmed it to match the existing test style and added the exact dependency wording.

findings.title: Metadata-stripping and rotation tests have no stated fixture method, no precondition and only check EXIF
findings.problem: 'A fixture JPEG with GPS EXIF' is not creatable from nothing without a decision (checked-in binary vs generated with sharp .withExif / a hand-built EXIF segment). Without asserting the fixture really contains GPS before processing, the test passes vacuously. The requirement also covers XMP, IPTC, ICC (convert to sRGB) and orientation, none of which are tested. 'No uploaded photo keeps location or camera metadata' is the headline security criterion, yet the test checks only sharp().metadata().exif and never the raw bytes. Rotate behaviour (orientation 6 swapping width and height, width/height stored for the 'largest copy') and the 40 MP limit fixture (a solid-colour 8000x6000 PNG, small in bytes) are also unspecified.
findings.evidence: Spec Testing: 'GPS removed: a fixture JPEG with GPS EXIF produces copies whose sharp().metadata() has no EXIF.' and Success criteria 'No uploaded photo keeps location or camera metadata.'
findings.fix:
Replace the line "GPS removed: a fixture JPEG with GPS EXIF produces copies whose `sharp().metadata()` has no EXIF." with:

"Metadata stripping: fixtures are generated in the test with sharp, with no committed binary needed. Create a 1200x900 JPEG with `.withExif({ IFD3: { GPSLatitude: '6/1,10/1,0/1', GPSLatitudeRef: 'S' } })`, an XMP packet (`.withXmp(...)`) and an ICC profile (`.withIccProfile('p3')`). A precondition assertion proves the input really carries `exif`, `xmp` and `icc` in `sharp().metadata()` and that the raw input buffer contains the bytes `Exif` and `GPS`, so the test cannot pass vacuously. For every output copy assert that `metadata().exif`, `xmp`, `iptc` and `orientation` are undefined. Assert that the WebP RIFF chunk list of the raw buffer contains no `EXIF` or `XMP ` chunk and that the buffer does not contain `<x:xmpmeta`. Assert that the colour space is sRGB: either no `ICCP` chunk is present or the profile is sRGB. Add a second generated fixture of 1200x900 with EXIF orientation 6 (`.withMetadata({ orientation: 6 })`): the largest copy must be stored with width 900 and height 1200, and the output has no orientation tag. Add a CMYK or Display-P3 fixture that is output as sRGB.

Add to the size-limit bullet: the 40 MP test uses a generated solid-colour PNG just over 40 megapixels (for example 8001x5000), which is only a few hundred KB in bytes. It must be refused with 422 `VALIDATION` through `limitInputPixels` before any pixel decoding or resizing, and no storage write may happen."
findings.verifyReason: Spec line 183 says only "a fixture JPEG with GPS EXIF produces copies whose sharp().metadata() has no EXIF", with no fixture method or precondition. Spec line 99 also requires XMP, IPTC and sRGB conversion, and line 98 requires orientation to be applied, and none of those has a test. The headline criterion (line 14) is therefore only checked through metadata().exif, which can pass vacuously. Rotation, the stored width/height of the largest copy, and the 40 MP fixture (line 92) are likewise unspecified. This is not a reversal of any approved owner decision, because the "GPS and all metadata stripped" decision is only being made testable. One correction to the proposed fix: asserting that the raw bytes contain "GPS" can give a false positive on compressed WebP data, so check the WebP RIFF chunk fourcc values instead.

findings.title: Reorder, delete and variant-link edge cases are unspecified: duplicates, foreign ids, empty or malformed body, gap closing under the unique key, concurrent delete and reorder
findings.problem: The spec says reorder 'must list exactly the product's current photo ids, otherwise 409' but not how duplicates ([a,a,b] with the right length), ids of another product's photos, an empty list on a product with photos, an unknown id, or a non-array/non-string body are handled (409 vs 422), and not whether another product's id leaks existence. Delete 'closes the gap in positions' in one transaction, but decrementing positions one by one collides with the unique key unless it uses the same +100 or ordered-update trick; this is not stated, so the implementer can ship a collision. Delete and reorder racing: the 'exactly current ids' comparison must be made inside the same transaction under a product row lock, otherwise a reorder validated before a concurrent delete writes a stale order. PUT /v1/admin/variants/:sku/image: unknown sku, unknown imageId (as opposed to another product's) and re-linking a variant to the same image have no row in the error table. A one-photo product (reorder of 1, delete of the last photo leaving the empty state, main photo promotion after deleting position 0) has no test.
findings.evidence: Spec: 'The body must list exactly the product's current photo ids, otherwise 409.' and 'delete the row ..., close the gap in positions and write the audit entry'; Error table has only 'Reorder list does not match | 409' and 'Variant links to another product's photo | 422'.
findings.fix:
Section 2, "Order of work", replace the Reorder and Delete bullets with:

- Reorder: one transaction that first locks the product row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, as the order lock does), then validates the body, then moves every photo of the product to `position + 100` and writes the final positions. Validation: `ids` must be an array of strings, otherwise 422 VALIDATION "Daftar urutan foto tidak valid." The set must equal the product's current photo ids with no duplicates. Anything else (duplicate, missing, extra, another product's id, unknown id, empty list on a product with photos) returns 409 CONFLICT "Urutan foto berubah. Muat ulang halaman." without saying which ids exist. An empty list on a product with no photos is a no-op that returns 200 and writes no audit entry.
- Delete: one transaction that locks the product row first, deletes the row (variant links clear through `onDelete: SetNull`), closes the gap with the same +100 two-step update, so positions end as 0..n-2 and the unique key never collides, and writes the audit entry. The photo that moves to position 0 becomes the main photo. Deleting the last photo leaves the empty state. The files are deleted after the commit. An unknown imageId, or one that belongs to another product, returns 404 NOT_FOUND "Foto tidak ditemukan." with the same text for both, so existence in another product is not revealed.
- Variant link (`PUT /v1/admin/variants/:sku/image`): 404 NOT_FOUND for an unknown sku. For an `imageId` that does not exist or belongs to another product, 422 VALIDATION "Foto tidak milik produk ini." (same text for both). Linking a variant to the photo it already has, or setting null when already null, returns 200 and writes no audit entry. Otherwise write VARIANT_IMAGE_LINKED.

Error table, add rows:
| Unknown product, photo or variant sku | 404 | `NOT_FOUND` | Data tidak ditemukan. |
| Unknown imageId on variant link | 422 | `VALIDATION` | Foto tidak milik produk ini. |
| Reorder body is not an array of strings | 422 | `VALIDATION` | Daftar urutan foto tidak valid. |

Testing, add to server unit tests:
- Reorder with duplicate ids ([a,a,b] with the right length), a foreign id, a missing id, an unknown id, and an empty list on a product with photos all return 409 with positions unchanged. A non-array body returns 422.
- A one-photo product: reorder of 1 succeeds, and delete of the only photo leaves the empty state.
- Delete of position 0 on a product with 4 photos promotes the next photo, and positions end as 0..2 without a unique-key error.
- Delete racing reorder on a fake database with a product lock gives one success and one 409, with positions still 0..n-1 and unique.
- Relinking a variant to a photo that was deleted returns 422. A variant link with an unknown sku returns 404. Re-linking to the same photo returns 200 with no new audit entry.
findings.verifyReason: The spec has real gaps, though the finding overstates some of them. Reorder: the rule "exactly the product's current photo ids, otherwise 409" already covers duplicates, foreign ids, missing ids and unknown ids, so those cases only need to be listed explicitly. A malformed body (not an array of strings) is the one unspecified status. Delete: the spec says "close the gap in positions" but never says how. Reorder spells out the +100 two-step, so a one-by-one decrement under @@unique([productId, position]) could collide. Locking: no section says the reorder and delete validations run under a product row lock, so a concurrent delete and reorder could write a stale order. Error table: it has no row for an unknown variant sku, an unknown imageId, or an unknown product. Testing: the cases listed in the finding (duplicate ids, one-photo product, delete of position 0, delete racing reorder, relinking after delete) are absent. The fix does not reverse any owner decision in "Item 1 decisions". I did not check whether a NOT_FOUND code already exists in the server's error codes.

findings.title: Alt text validation is ambiguous for whitespace, emoji and HTML, and the PATCH alt route has no stated rule
findings.section: 1. Data (alt) / 2. Checks on upload step 6 / Error messages
findings.problem: 'Trimmed, 1–125 characters' has two readings for emoji and combining characters (JS string length counts UTF-16 units, so 70 emoji exceed 125; Postgres counts code points; users see graphemes). 'Trimmed' does not say whether an alt of only spaces, tabs, NBSP, zero-width spaces or newlines counts as empty. HTML such as '<script>' or '<' has no rule (store verbatim and rely on React escaping, or reject), and the value is later written into aria-label and audit before/after JSON. The error-table row 'Alt text missing or too long' is specified only for upload; PATCH and the admin form prefill 'Foto {nama produk}' (which can itself exceed 125 characters for a long product name) are not covered. Each ambiguity gives a different test outcome.
findings.evidence: Spec step 6: 'Alt text: trimmed, 1–125 characters. The admin form prefills "Foto {nama produk}".' Table: 'Alt text missing or too long | 422 | VALIDATION'.
findings.fix: Replace step 6 of "2. Upload, processing and access control" with: "6. Alt text (upload and PATCH, one shared function): strip leading and trailing Unicode whitespace and zero-width characters (including NBSP, U+200B, U+200D, U+FEFF); replace tabs, line breaks and other control characters inside the text with a single space. Length is counted in Unicode code points and must be 1 to 125. Empty after cleaning, or over 125, returns 422 VALIDATION 'Teks alternatif wajib diisi (1–125 karakter).'. HTML is stored as plain text, not stripped and not rejected, and is only ever shown as text (React escaping; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML; no raw HTML in aria-label). Audit before/after values hold the stored string as JSON. The admin form prefill 'Foto {nama produk}' is cut at 125 code points." In the error table, change the row label to "Alt text missing or too long (upload and PATCH)". Add to Testing (server unit tests): - alt values " ", a string of NBSP and zero-width characters only, and "\n\t" are all refused - exactly 125 and 126 code points - 125 emoji accepted, 126 refused - "" stored verbatim and rendered as text - PATCH applies the same rules - prefill from a 140-character product name is cut to 125 code points Add to Web unit tests: the alt input counter counts code points, not UTF-16 units.
findings.verifyReason: The spec text matches the finding. Step 6 of the upload checks says only "trimmed, 1–125 characters". It does not define "trimmed" (NBSP, zero-width characters, newlines), the unit of length (UTF-16 units, code points or graphemes), or what happens to HTML. The PATCH route is listed as "Change alt text" with no validation rule, and the error table gives no scope for the alt row. The prefill "Foto {nama produk}" has no length cut, so a long product name can break the 125 limit on first save. The 1–125 limit and the "Foto {nama produk}" default are approved owner decisions and stay unchanged. The fix only defines how they are applied, so it does not reverse any decision. I would drop NFC normalisation from the finding's fix: it is not needed, and it changes stored text without a stated reason. The control-character handling and the zero-width trim are worth keeping.

findings.title: Variant/catalogue tests cannot detect the SetNull and dangling-link behaviour, and the storefront gallery rules have unspecified cases
findings.section: 1. Data and storage (Variant.imageId) / 4. Storefront gallery / Testing
findings.problem: The test 'delete clearing a variant link' is vacuous on a fake that does not implement onDelete: SetNull; only a real Postgres (or an explicit service-level update) would prove it. The spec relies on the database alone, so a test on the fake would assert nothing about the real constraint, and 'prisma db push' on an existing table of seeded variants is not exercised either. Catalogue logic with a variant whose imageId points to a photo missing from product.images (stale cache within the 15 s window, or after deletion), a product with one photo and a variant linked to it (no thumbnail row, but the variant must still select it), and variants with no linked photo falling back to the previous or main photo when the shopper switches variant are not specified, so the gallery unit test 'picks the variant's photo' has no defined expected result for these cases.
findings.evidence: Spec: 'Variant gains imageId String? with a relation to ProductImage and onDelete: SetNull'; Testing: 'delete clearing a variant link'; Storefront: 'Picking a variant with a linked photo switches the main photo and presses its thumbnail; pressing a thumbnail does not change the variant.' fake-db.ts has no cascade logic (lines 15-35).
findings.fix:
Section 2, Delete bullet, add after "(variant links clear through `onDelete: SetNull`)": "The service also clears variant links explicitly in the same transaction (`variant.updateMany` where `imageId` = the deleted id, set to null) so the behaviour is covered by unit tests on the fake database; the `onDelete: SetNull` relation stays as a backstop for any other delete path."

Section 4, Storefront, add a bullet after the gallery bullet: "Gallery selection rules: (a) First render shows the linked photo of the default variant if it is present in `product.images`, otherwise position 0. (b) Picking a variant whose `imageId` is missing from `product.images` (stale catalogue within the 15-second cache, or the photo was just deleted), or that has no `imageId`, leaves the currently shown photo unchanged; it never falls back to the drawing while the product still has photos. (c) A product with one photo shows that photo and no thumbnail row, even when a variant links to it; the variant selection is still honoured (no change needed). (d) Pressing a thumbnail never changes the variant."

Testing, server unit tests: replace "delete clearing a variant link" with "delete clears variant links through the explicit updateMany (fake database), and `PUT /v1/admin/variants/:sku/image` refuses a photo of another product". Web unit tests, add cases: "variant with a linked photo switches main photo and pressed thumbnail; variant with an imageId not in product.images or with none keeps the current photo; first render uses the default variant's linked photo else position 0; one-photo product with a linked variant shows the photo and no thumbnail row".

Testing, On dev, add: "Real-database check: link a variant to a photo, delete that photo in admin; the variant's `imageId` is null in Postgres (proves SetNull), `GET /v1/products/:slug` shows no `imageId` on that variant after the 15-second cache, and the storefront variant switch keeps showing the main photo. Also confirm `prisma db push` on the existing seeded Variant table adds the nullable `imageId` column without data loss."
findings.verifyReason: Checked the spec and server/src/test/fake-db.ts. The fake has no cascade, SetNull or delete logic (grep finds none). The spec's Testing line "delete clearing a variant link" and its Delete bullet rely only on onDelete: SetNull, so a fake-db test would prove nothing about the constraint. The spec also leaves the gallery cases undefined: a variant whose imageId is missing from product.images (stale 15 s cache or after deletion), a one-photo product with a linked variant, and a variant with no linked photo. Section 4 says only "Picking a variant with a linked photo switches the main photo", so the "picks the variant's photo" unit test has no expected result for those cases. The fix does not reverse any Item 1 decision (variant link, thumbnails under the main photo, drawing fallback all stay). I made two changes to the reviewer's fix. First, the explicit updateMany keeps SetNull as a backstop. Second, a real-DB check is added for the Postgres behaviour, because the fake cannot prove it. "No flicker to the drawing" is reworded as "unchanged photo". The "one photo = no thumbnail row" rule is kept as already stated; only the variant-selection rule is added.

findings.title: media:seed and media:remove-samples have no defined actor or audit codes, and seed re-adds samples after a client deleted them
findings.section: 5. Demo photos, credits and removal; 2. Audit codes
findings.problem: Constraint 7 and Prompt.md rule 9 require every admin mutation to write an append-only audit entry with actor, time, action, object, before and after. The spec writes audit entries only for the staff endpoints. `remove-samples` is a bulk delete of customer-visible content run from a CLI, where there is no staff cookie, and the spec says only 'with audit entries' (no code, actor, or before/after). `media:seed` writes rows with `createdBy: "seed"` and no audit at all. Also seed 'adds rows only to products that have no photos yet': a client that deliberately removed all photos of a product and re-runs the seed (or a deploy script that runs it every time) gets sample photos back silently. The existing audit store keeps actor as a free-text name (admin.service.ts:167 actor() and AuditRecord.actor String), not a staff id, so 'createdBy: Staff id' also differs from how audit attributes actors.
findings.evidence: Spec line 154: 'uploads missing files and adds rows ... only to products that have no photos yet'; line 155: 'deletes every sample photo (rows and files) with audit entries'; line 110 lists only five audit codes, none for seed/remove. server/prisma/schema.prisma:122-131 `model AuditRecord { actor String ... }`; server/src/commerce/admin.service.ts:167 `private actor(user: { name: string; role: StaffRole })`.
findings.fix:
Section 2, replace the audit codes line with: "Audit codes, each with actor, time, object (`productId`), before and after (the photo list): `PRODUCT_IMAGE_ADDED`, `PRODUCT_IMAGE_REMOVED`, `PRODUCT_IMAGE_REORDERED`, `PRODUCT_IMAGE_ALT_CHANGED`, `VARIANT_IMAGE_LINKED`, `PRODUCT_IMAGE_SAMPLE_SEEDED`, `PRODUCT_IMAGE_SAMPLES_REMOVED`. The audit actor is the same free-text name string the existing audit store uses (`actor()` in admin.service.ts, `AuditRecord.actor`)."

Section 1, `createdBy` row: "Same actor string as the audit entry (the staff member's name, as `actor()` produces it), or `seed` for sample photos."

Section 5, replace the media:seed and media:remove-samples bullets with:
- "`npm run media:seed` (inside the API container on a server) uploads missing files and adds rows with `source: \"sample\"` and `createdBy: \"seed\"` only to products that have no photos yet AND have no earlier `PRODUCT_IMAGE_REMOVED` or `PRODUCT_IMAGE_SAMPLES_REMOVED` audit entry, so a photo removal by a client is never undone by a re-run or a deploy script. It never changes or removes a client's uploads, and running it twice changes nothing. findings.title: Photo rights checklist is incomplete: property releases, artwork, product design and licence-text verification are not covered; Unsplash and Pexels terms not stated
findings.problem: The rejection list covers visible brands/logos and identifiable people (model releases), but not property releases (buildings, interiors, artworks, or distinctive product designs and packaging shapes that can be protected), nor 'photo contains another work' (posters, screens, book covers). A CC licence from the uploader does not clear third-party rights in the depicted subject; Commons marks these with templates other than the two listed (for example {{Non-free}}, {{FoP-...}}). The spec lists Unsplash and Pexels licence (no credit) but their licences exclude using the photo to imply endorsement or in a way that shows people or trademarks in a bad light, and prohibit selling unaltered copies or compiling to compete with their services; our 'committed to the repo and distributed with the template to clients' reuse is a redistribution of the files, which both licences allow only as part of a product, not as a standalone set. The spec also does not record the licence verification (date, licence version, the exact page text) that would prove the licence at the time of download, nor does it fix the licence version (CC BY 4.0 vs 2.0/3.0, which have different attribution details).

A CC licence from the uploader does not clear third-party rights in the depicted subject, so check the subject as well as the licence."

Add after line 150: "Accepted CC versions: CC0 1.0, Public Domain Mark, CC BY 2.0, 3.0 or 4.0, CC BY-SA 4.0 (3.0 only if nothing else fits). The exact version is recorded per photo, and the credit text follows that version's attribution rules (creator, title, source link, licence link, and a note if the photo was changed; our resizing and cropping counts as a change). Unsplash and Pexels photos are used only as sample images inside the template and are never offered as a standalone set. Their licences do not allow implying endorsement or showing people or trademarks in a bad light."

Add fields to the sample-photo records (samples.json, and the ProductImage record for sample photos): `licenceVersion` (String?), `retrievedAt` (WIB date, set when the file was downloaded) and `licenceCheck` (String?: who checked, plus the licence text or template seen on the source page at that time). Appendix A (the photo list) records, for each photo, the source URL, creator, licence and version, retrievedAt, and the checker's initials, so the licence can be shown as it stood on download day."

The handoff's Item 1 decisions already require free licences, no NC/ND, "sample sources recorded" and a stripped, replaceable sample set, and the fix tightens how those are applied. findings.title: Delete 'closes the gap' collides with the (productId, position) unique key
findings.section: 2. Upload, processing and access control (Order of work, Delete)
findings.problem: Reorder is carefully written to avoid unique collisions (move to position+100 first). Delete says only 'close the gap in positions', which is a set of position updates on the same unique key. A single UPDATE position = position - 1 on a non-deferrable unique index can fail in PostgreSQL depending on row order. The spec is also inconsistent about the range: position is declared 'Int (0-5)' but reorder temporarily writes up to 105, and no CHECK constraint is specified, so the stated range is only an application rule.
findings.evidence: spec section 1: '`position` | `Int` (0-5)... `@@unique([productId, position])`'; reorder: 'moves every photo... to `position + 100`'; delete: 'close the gap in positions and write the audit entry'
findings.fix:
Section 2, Delete (line 107): replace "close the gap in positions" with "close the gap with the same two-step method as Reorder, inside the same transaction: after deleting the row, move the remaining photos of the product to `position + 100`, then write final positions 0..n-1 in their previous order".

Section 1, `position` row (line 40): replace "`Int` (0-5)" with "`Int`, 0-5 in committed data (temporarily up to +100 inside a reorder or delete transaction; the range is enforced by the API, not by a database CHECK)".

Tests section: add "Deleting the middle photo of four leaves positions 0,1,2 in the previous order with no unique-key error. Deleting the main photo promotes the next photo to position 0."
findings.verifyReason: Spec line 107 says only "close the gap in positions" for Delete. Line 106 uses the two-step +100 method for Reorder because `@@unique([productId, position])` (line 40) is a non-deferrable PostgreSQL index, which checks each row as it is updated. A bulk `UPDATE ... SET position = position - 1` can therefore fail depending on row order. Ascending single-row updates after the delete would avoid the collision, but the spec does not say so, so the ordering is left to the implementer. The range wording is also inconsistent. Line 40 says `Int (0-5)`, while Reorder writes values up to 105 and no CHECK constraint is specified. The fix does not reverse any owner decision: the handoff's Item 1 decisions only cap photos at 6 and say nothing about how positions are rewritten. Severity is closer to minor than major, because deleting the row first makes ascending updates safe.

findings.title: media:seed and remove-samples cannot run in the API container as the Dockerfile is written; seed data is under-specified
