In section 5, replace the last sentence of the bullet at line 153 and the bullets at lines 154-155 with:

"- The scripts are TypeScript in `server/src/media/cli/seed.ts` and `server/src/media/cli/remove-samples.ts`. The admin banner and a new "Before launch" item in `docs/07-delivery/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md` both point to it. Both scripts are run with `docker compose exec api npm run ...`.

findings.title: Upload validation and error table disagree and omit cases

findings.title: MinIO outage at API start can crash-loop the whole API, including checkout, and the spec adds more start-up MinIO work
findings.section: 1. Data and storage (bucket policy at start-up) / Rollout on dev
findings.problem: ObjectStorage.onModuleInit awaits ensureBucket(), which treats ANY HeadBucket error (network down, bad credentials) as 'bucket missing' and then calls CreateBucket, which also throws. The exception propagates out of Nest bootstrap, so the API does not start while MinIO is down or restarting. Today MinIO only backs /health, but the spec adds a policy call to the same hook and makes MinIO the only store for product photos. Orders, payments and stock all live in Postgres and need MinIO not at all, yet a MinIO restart or a wrong key in one client's server/.env would take checkout offline. The spec names a 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE for requests but says nothing about start-up, retries or readiness.
findings.evidence: server/src/storage.service.ts:22-32: `async onModuleInit() { await this.ensureBucket(); }` and `try { HeadBucket } catch { await CreateBucket }`; spec line 57: 'At start-up the API sets a bucket policy...'; spec line 172 only covers 503 on requests.
findings.fix: Add to section 1 after the bucket-policy bullet: "Start-up must never block checkout on MinIO. ObjectStorage.onModuleInit catches every error from ensureBucket and from the policy call. It logs one structured line (event=storage_init_failed, error class only, no keys or endpoint credentials), sets ready=false and lets the API start. ensureBucket calls CreateBucket only when HeadBucket fails with NotFound/404 (NoSuchBucket); any other error (network, auth, 5xx) is treated as 'storage unavailable' and never triggers CreateBucket. The init retries every 30 s until bucket and policy are both in place, then sets ready=true and logs storage_init_ok once. While ready=false, upload, delete and media:seed return 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE (same copy as the request-time 503 in the error table). Catalogue, cart, checkout, payments and stock are unaffected. GET /health reports storage: degraded with HTTP 200 instead of failing. Add unit tests: (a) a storage stub whose HeadBucket/CreateBucket/policy calls throw leaves onModuleInit resolved with ready=false; (b) a non-404 HeadBucket error does not call CreateBucket; (c) a later successful retry sets ready=true."
findings.verifyReason: Checked server/src/storage.service.ts lines 22-32. onModuleInit awaits ensureBucket(). ensureBucket sends HeadBucket and, on ANY error, sends CreateBucket without catching it. With MinIO down, or with bad keys, both calls throw, the error escapes Nest bootstrap, and the API fails to start. Orders and stock use only Postgres, so checkout goes down with it. The spec (line 57) adds a bucket-policy call at start-up in the same hook. Its only failure handling is a 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE for requests (line 172). It says nothing about start-up failure, retry or readiness, and a grep for "health" finds only the private health/ prefix at line 57, so there is no readiness behaviour either. Nothing in the finding reverses an owner decision, and it is a robustness requirement, not a style preference.

findings.title: No rollout order or rollback plan for the schema, API and nginx changes
findings.problem: Rollout is three steps with no ordering constraint between api and web, and no rollback. The web image (new nginx /media location, 11m body limit) and the API image (new tables, new catalogue fields) deploy independently. If the web image is rebuilt before MinIO policy is applied, or the API is rolled back after media:seed ran, the catalogue/admin screens and /media disagree. The new ProductImage table and Variant.imageId column stay after a rollback of the API image (prisma db push does not drop), and an old API image started against a database with the extra column and a table whose relations it does not know is untested. The spec lists no 'before' backup of the media bucket and says nothing about what to do if the seed or the post-deploy checks fail.
findings.evidence: spec lines 202-206: '1. Deploy as before (back up, upload source, rebuild api and web); nginx -t ... 2. docker compose exec api npm run media:seed. 3. Run the checks above.' No rollback step anywhere in the spec.
findings.fix:
Replace the "Rollout on dev" section with:

## Rollout on dev

1. Before deploying: back up Postgres as before, and save a dated listing of the media bucket (`mc ls --recursive`) so uploads can be compared after a failure.
2. Deploy `api` first (new table, nullable `Variant.imageId`, bucket policy at start-up). Confirm `/health` reports storage ok and that anonymous GET of a `media/*` object works while `GET /media/` stays 404. Then deploy `web` (new `/media/` location, `client_max_body_size 11m`), running `nginx -t` on the compose network before restarting.
3. `docker compose exec api npm run media:seed`.
4. Run the checks above.

Order rule: never deploy `web` before `api`. The storefront treats a product whose `images` is empty or missing the same as a photo that fails to load, and shows the drawing. Rolling back `web` alone is therefore safe.

Rollback: redeploy the previous `api` image. The new table and the nullable column are additive, so the old code ignores them. Before the first deploy, start the previous image once against a copy of the dev database with the new schema and confirm the catalogue and checkout still respond. Never drop `ProductImage` or `Variant.imageId` as part of a rollback. Uploaded files and rows stay in place and are reused when the new version is redeployed.

If `media:seed` fails halfway, run it again, since it is idempotent. If a clean state is needed, run `npm run media:remove-samples` and then `media:seed`. If a post-deploy check fails, stop, record the failing check in the deploy notes, and roll back `web` first, then `api` if the failure is on the API side.
findings.verifyReason: The spec's "Rollout on dev" (lines 202-206) has three steps and no order between api and web. It has no rollback, and no instruction for when media:seed or the checks fail. Step 1 already says "back up", so the reviewer's claim of no backup is partly wrong, but it does not cover the media bucket. The schema change is additive (a new table and a nullable Variant.imageId), so an old API should ignore it, but the spec never says so. The risk is limited because this is dev only, and the fix does not reverse any Item 1 decision. One part of the proposed fix is wrong: it asserts "verified" for an old-image test that has not been run, and the fallback to the drawing for an empty or missing images list is not stated in the spec at line 175, which only covers photos that fail to load. The refined text below drops the unverified claim and adds that fallback explicitly.

findings.title: Media files have no backup or restore story, yet the database rows point at them and originals are discarded

findings.title: New config and defaults per client fork are not listed (.env.example, compose, limits)
findings.problem: CLAUDE.md says each client is an independent fork configured through env files. The spec adds values that are hard-coded or implicit: MINIO_BUCKET into the web container, the upstream host and port (host.docker.internal:9000 is hard-coded in nginx and differs from MINIO_ENDPOINT, which a fork could set to another host or port), 10 MB / 6 photos / 480 px / 40 MP limits, and quality 80. A fork with a MinIO on another host or port gets a /media that points to the wrong place while uploads still work, so photos show the drawing everywhere with no error. server/.env.example does not list anything new and the spec does not say which of these are configurable.
findings.evidence: server/.env.example:4-7 lists MINIO_ENDPOINT, MINIO_ACCESS_KEY, MINIO_SECRET_KEY, MINIO_BUCKET, MINIO_REGION only; spec line 114 hard-codes `http://host.docker.internal:9000/${MINIO_BUCKET}/media/`.
findings.fix:
Add this subsection to section 3 (Serving and caching), titled "Configuration per client fork":

1. nginx upstream. The /media/ location proxies to `${MEDIA_UPSTREAM}/${MINIO_BUCKET}/media/`.
   - `MEDIA_UPSTREAM` is the MinIO origin as seen from the web container, with no path. Default: `http://host.docker.internal:9000`.
   - `MINIO_BUCKET` defaults to `tian-media`.
   - Both are set under the web service `environment:` in docker-compose.yml with these defaults, for example `MEDIA_UPSTREAM: ${MEDIA_UPSTREAM:-http://host.docker.internal:9000}` and `MINIO_BUCKET: ${MINIO_BUCKET:-tian-media}`. Both are documented in the root `.env.example`.
   - The compose default is required because the nginx template's envsubst only fills variables that are set. Without a default, an unset MEDIA_UPSTREAM would give nginx a broken proxy_pass.
   - A fork whose MinIO is on another host or port must set MEDIA_UPSTREAM to match its `MINIO_ENDPOINT` in server/.env. The root `.env.example` comment says the two values must point to the same MinIO.
2. Limits. These are constants in `server/src/media/limits.ts`: max file 10 MB, max photos per product 6, min shorter side 480 px, max 40 megapixels, WebP quality 80, widths 480/960/1600.
   - They are not env vars, so every fork behaves the same. Changing them needs a code change.
   - A changed max file size also needs a matching change to nginx `client_max_body_size` on `location /v1/` (limit plus 1 MB).
3. Fail loudly. `media:seed` and the post-deploy check request `/media/{key of a known sample photo}` through the web origin. If it does not return 200, they stop with the message "Gambar tidak dapat dimuat lewat /media; periksa MEDIA_UPSTREAM dan MINIO_BUCKET." They also print the upstream URL that was used.
4. server/.env.example gets no new keys, because nothing server-side is new. The spec states that explicitly.
findings.verifyReason: The spec (lines 114-115) hard-codes the nginx upstream as http://host.docker.internal:9000/${MINIO_BUCKET}/media/ and passes only MINIO_BUCKET to the web service. server/.env.example:4 makes MINIO_ENDPOINT configurable per fork, so a fork with MinIO on another host or port gets a /media route that points to the wrong place. Uploads would still work through the API, but photo URLs would fail and every product would show the drawing fallback, with no error raised. The limits (10 MB, 6 photos, 480 px, 40 MP, quality 80, and the 11m nginx body size at line 117) are fixed in the spec without saying whether they are constants or configuration. Nothing in the spec or in server/.env.example lists the new values. I did not find an owner decision that this fix would reverse. One refinement: nginx envsubst only fills variables that exist in the container environment, so the compose file must set a default for MEDIA_UPSTREAM, or nginx would receive an empty value. Also, MEDIA_UPSTREAM is the web container's own variable and is not the same as the API's MINIO_ENDPOINT. The same value should be kept in one place so the two cannot drift.

findings.title: No logging or observability for upload, processing and storage failures, and the audit log is the only trace
findings.section: 2. Upload, processing and access control / Error messages
findings.problem: The spec defines audit entries for successful changes but no operational log for the things most likely to fail in production: sharp errors, MinIO put/delete failures, compensation deletes that themselves fail (orphans), rejected uploads and their reasons, duration and size per upload. The only operational trace the debugging section of CLAUDE.md gives is SQL on tables. A failed delete 'only leaves an unlinked file' with no record of which file, so the deferred cleanup job could never find them. The existing server has almost no logger usage.
findings.evidence: spec line 107: 'A failed file delete only leaves an unlinked file.' and line 218 defers an orphan-cleanup job; grep of server/src shows Logger/console only in catalog.service.ts and reservation-sweeper.ts.
findings.fix:
Add to section 2, after the "Order of work" list (after line 108):

"Operational log. Every upload, delete and compensation writes one structured Nest `Logger` line (no new dependency, no new table). Fields: `event`, `productId`, `imageId` (when known), `staffId`, `bytes`, `durationMs`, and for failures `errorClass` and `leftBehindKeys` (the MinIO object keys that were not removed or not written). Events: `media_upload_ok`, `media_upload_rejected` (with the rule that failed: type, size, pixels, count, alt text, duplicate or permission), `media_processing_failed`, `storage_unavailable`, `media_delete_files_failed` and `media_compensation_failed`. The last two are logged at error level with the full key list, so the orphan-file cleanup deferred to a later round can be built from the log. Never log file contents, client-supplied filenames, alt text or credentials. This log supplements the audit trail and does not replace it: the audit log stays the only record of who changed what."

Add a test line to section 7: "A failed compensation delete and a failed post-delete file removal each emit the error-level event with the key list."
findings.verifyReason: I read the spec (lines 84-118 and a grep for log, orphan and Logger). It has no operational logging requirement. Line 107 says a failed file delete "only leaves an unlinked file" and records nothing. Line 105 says files are deleted again if the transaction fails, with no record if that delete fails too. Line 218 defers an orphan-cleanup job, and with no key list logged there would be nothing for it to build on. The audit codes at line 110 only cover successful changes. The grep of server/src finds Logger or console only in reservation-sweeper.ts and catalog.service.ts, so the finding's evidence holds. The gap is real but modest, so "major" is somewhat high. The fix reverses no owner decision, since it adds logging only. I tightened the fix: Nest Logger only, no new table, no new dependency, and error-level logging of the full key list on failed cleanup.

findings.title: Removing a photo does not remove it from public reach: one-year immutable caches and unlinked files stay anonymously readable
findings.problem: The spec calls an unlinked file after a failed file delete 'harmless', but the bucket policy allows anonymous GET on every media/* key and no cleanup job is planned this round, so a photo removed because it was wrong, contained a person, or carried a licence problem remains retrievable by anyone who has its URL (it was public with a 1-year immutable header, so it also persists in shared caches and browsers). The owner decision 'one-year cache' is kept; what is missing is an honest statement of that limit and a retry for the delete.
findings.evidence: spec: 'A failed file delete only leaves an unlinked file.' and Risks: 'Unlinked files after a failed delete: harmless (nothing links to them)'; Not in this round: 'an orphan-file cleanup job'.
findings.fix:
1) In section 2, "Order of work", replace the Delete bullet's last sentence ("A failed file delete only leaves an unlinked file.") with: "Delete the files after the transaction commits, retrying each failed file removal up to 3 times. If a file still cannot be deleted, write a separate append-only audit entry PRODUCT_IMAGE_FILE_DELETE_FAILED (actor, time, object productId, after = the list of undeleted keys) so staff can remove the files by hand. The photo is already removed from the storefront and the catalogue at that point; only the file remains."

2) In section 2, add `PRODUCT_IMAGE_FILE_DELETE_FAILED` to the audit codes list. Add a server unit test: a file delete that fails 3 times yields one PRODUCT_IMAGE_FILE_DELETE_FAILED entry listing the keys, and the row stays removed.

3) Replace the Risks bullet "Unlinked files after a failed delete: harmless (nothing links to them); a cleanup job is listed below as later work." with: "A removed photo stays fetchable by anyone who holds its URL until its files are deleted, because the bucket policy allows anonymous reads of media/*. Browsers and any shared cache that already stored it keep it for up to a year (the approved one-year immutable cache is unchanged). Delete retries the file removal 3 times and, if it still fails, records PRODUCT_IMAGE_FILE_DELETE_FAILED with the keys for manual removal; an automatic cleanup job stays out of this round. A photo with a privacy or licence problem must not be uploaded in the first place; the upload area says so in one line."

4) In section 4, "Upload area" bullet, add this line under the rules text: "Jangan unggah foto yang memuat orang yang dapat dikenali atau yang lisensinya tidak jelas. Foto yang sudah dihapus masih dapat diakses lewat tautannya selama file-nya belum terhapus dan dapat tersimpan di cache peramban hingga 1 tahun."
findings.verifyReason: Verified in the spec. Line 57 sets anonymous s3:GetObject on media/*. Line 116 sends a one-year immutable cache header. Line 107 says a failed file delete "only leaves an unlinked file". Line 213 calls that "harmless". Line 218 defers an orphan-file cleanup job. A removed photo therefore stays readable by anyone who has its URL, and cached copies live up to a year. This does not reverse an owner decision, because the one-year cache and the Owner/Admin/Marketing roles stay as approved. The real defect is that the spec calls the leftover harmless and gives no retry or trace for the delete. The reviewer's fix needs three corrections. Its new audit code is missing from the audit-code list at line 110. The upload-screen warning needs Bahasa Indonesia copy, since constraint 9 requires it. The audit entry should be written after the file delete fails, because the row and its PRODUCT_IMAGE_REMOVED entry are already committed by then. This is minor severity because the URLs contain an unguessable 16-hex hash and the nginx /media location has no shared proxy cache.

findings.title: Metadata-stripping and content-type tests are too narrow to prove the 'no metadata' success criterion
findings.problem: The test only asserts that sharp().metadata() on the output shows no EXIF. Metadata() does not prove the absence of XMP, IPTC, an embedded thumbnail or an ICC profile in the bytes, and a stripped-input test would pass trivially if the fixture lacks them. The spec also does not say what Content-Type the stored objects get: ObjectStorage.putText hard-codes text/plain, and a new putImage must set image/webp so a stored object can never be served with a sniffable or HTML type. The credit link built from sourceUrl is rendered as an anchor with no rule on scheme or rel.
findings.evidence: server/src/storage.service.ts:39 `ContentType: "text/plain; charset=utf-8"`; spec Testing: 'copies whose `sharp().metadata()` has no EXIF'; spec section 4: 'linked to the source page'.
findings.fix:
Replace the Testing bullet "GPS removed: a fixture JPEG with GPS EXIF produces copies whose `sharp().metadata()` has no EXIF." with: "Metadata removed: the fixture JPEG carries GPS EXIF, an EXIF thumbnail, an XMP packet, IPTC and an embedded ICC profile (the test first asserts that sharp().metadata() on the INPUT reports exif, xmp, iptc and icc, so the fixture cannot pass trivially). For every output copy, sharp().metadata() must report no exif, xmp, iptc or icc, and the raw WebP bytes are parsed as a RIFF container: the chunk list may contain only VP8, VP8L, VP8X and ALPH/ANIM-free image chunks, and must contain none of the FourCCs EXIF, XMP or ICCP. The raw bytes must also not contain the strings GPSLatitude or http://ns.adobe.com/xap."

Add to section 2, after the Processing bullets: "Storage writes. A new `ObjectStorage.putImage(key, body)` stores each WebP copy with `ContentType: image/webp`; `putText` keeps text/plain for the health check only and is never used for photos. The seed script uses the same `putImage`. Unit test: the fake S3 client records ContentType, and every stored photo key must have image/webp. Public caching headers stay set by nginx (section 3), not on the object."

Add to section 4, in the credit bullet: "The credit text links to `sourceUrl` only when it starts with `https://` (checked in the API when the seed row is written and again in `ProductPhoto`'s credit line); otherwise the credit is shown as plain text. The anchor always has `target=\"_blank\"` and `rel=\"noopener noreferrer\"`. Web unit test: a sourceUrl of `javascript:alert(1)` or `http://…` renders no anchor."
findings.verifyReason: The spec never states a Content-Type for stored images. The only upload helper, putText in server/src/storage.service.ts:39, hard-codes "text/plain; charset=utf-8", and the spec's new upload path does not say it must differ. The credit link from sourceUrl has no scheme or rel rule. The metadata claim is only partly right. Stripping is already specified (no withMetadata/keepMetadata), and sharp's metadata() does report exif, icc, iptc and xmp buffers, so it is not blind to XMP or IPTC. The test is still too narrow, because it only names EXIF and a fixture without those blocks would pass trivially. The reviewer's byte-scan strings are wrong for WebP output. WebP is a RIFF container whose metadata chunks have the FourCCs EXIF, XMP and ICCP, so "Photoshop 3.0", "http://ns.adobe.com/xap" and "ICC_PROFILE" are JPEG-style markers that would never appear and the scan would pass vacuously. The fix below corrects this. Cache-Control is already set by nginx (section 3), so it is dropped from the fix. This is not an owner-decision reversal.

findings.title: MinIO failure handling is incomplete: partial writes, failed compensation, and where 503 applies
findings.section: 2. Upload (Order of work) and Error messages
findings.problem: Three WebP files are written one after another, but the spec only compensates when the database transaction fails. If the second or third PUT fails, the first files are left with no row and no cleanup; if the compensating delete itself fails nothing says what the user sees. STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE 503 is listed for 'MinIO unreachable' without saying that it also covers a failed PUT mid-upload (nothing saved) and a failed file delete after a committed delete (must stay 200). The start-up bucket policy step has no stated behaviour when MinIO is down at boot.
findings.evidence: spec L105 'write the WebP files to MinIO; then in one transaction ...; if the transaction fails, delete the files again'; L107 'A failed file delete only leaves an unlinked file'; L57 'At start-up the API sets a bucket policy'.
findings.fix:
Add under "Order of work" (after the Upload bullet at L105): "If any PUT fails, delete the keys this request already wrote (best effort, logged), insert no row, write no audit entry and answer 503 `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE`. If the transaction fails, the same best-effort delete applies. A failed compensating delete is logged and does not change the response. After a committed photo delete (L107), a failed file delete is logged and the response stays 200. At start-up, if MinIO is unreachable or the bucket policy cannot be set, the API logs the error and still starts. Every upload and delete first checks that the policy has been applied in this process and retries it if not. While it cannot be set, uploads answer 503 `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` and public `/media/` reads fail as plain 404."

Also amend the L172 error row to: "MinIO unreachable, a failed PUT during upload, or the bucket policy not yet applied | 503 | `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` | Penyimpanan foto sedang tidak tersedia. Coba lagi sebentar. (Nothing is saved.)" Add to the Tests list: "second PUT fails: first key deleted, no row, no audit entry, 503."
findings.verifyReason: Spec L105 compensates only when the DB transaction fails. It says nothing about a failed 2nd or 3rd of the three sequential PUTs, which would leave orphan WebP files with no row, or about a failed compensating delete. L172 lists 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE only for "MinIO unreachable". L57 sets the bucket policy at start-up with no behaviour if MinIO is down at boot. L107 implies, but does not state, that a failed file delete after a committed delete stays 200. No approved Item 1 decision is reversed, and best-effort cleanup fits the L218 exclusion of an orphan-file cleanup job. The reviewer's retry wording ("first successful upload retries the policy") is imprecise, so the fix below ties the retry to every upload until the policy is set.

findings.title: sizes values do not match the real layouts: Catalog grid is 2 columns up to 1023 px, thumbnails are 48 px and cart/account rows are 56, 72 and 80 px, not 64 px
findings.problem: Catalog.tsx uses `grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 xl:grid-cols-4` (and a 220 px sidebar layout), but the spec's `(min-width: 768px) 25vw` assumes 4 columns from 768 px. findings.title: Catalogue freshness claim is wrong (15 s becomes up to 60 s) and deleting a photo leaves cached catalogue pointing at deleted files
findings.section: 2. Order of work / 3. Serving and caching
findings.problem: The spec says after a change the storefront sees it 'within the 15-second catalogue cache'. cache-policy.ts sends max-age=15 plus stale-while-revalidate=45, so a browser can show the old catalogue for about 60 s (the file's own comment says 'about a minute'). Because Delete removes the files right after the transaction, a shopper with the old JSON requests a now-missing /media/... file, gets 404 and sees the drawing (via onError), which is OK for the shopper but is unlisted behaviour and makes the 'fallback only for products without photo' goal untrue for a minute. Photos also stay in browsers for a year after removal (immutable), which matters for a takedown of a wrongly licensed sample photo.
findings.evidence: server/src/cache-policy.ts:12 `public, max-age=15, stale-while-revalidate=45`; cache-policy.ts:4 'Catalogue stock may then lag about a minute'; spec section 2: "so the storefront sees it within the 15-second catalogue cache"
findings.fix:
Section 2, line 108: replace "so the storefront sees it within the 15-second catalogue cache" with "so the storefront sees it within about 60 seconds (catalogue `max-age=15` plus `stale-while-revalidate=45` in `cache-policy.ts`)".

Section 2, under Delete, add: "Files of a removed photo are deleted at once. A shopper whose cached catalogue still lists it gets a 404 for the file and sees the drawing through `onError` until the catalogue refreshes (at most about 60 s). Browsers that already loaded the file keep it for up to one year (`immutable`), so a licence takedown cannot be forced on returning visitors. The launch checklist states this."

Testing section, add: "After deleting a photo, the product page falls back to the drawing without a console error loop."
findings.verifyReason: The code confirms the freshness claim is wrong. cache-policy.ts line 12 sends max-age=15 plus stale-while-revalidate=45, and its own comment says stock may lag about a minute. Spec line 108 says the storefront sees changes within the 15-second catalogue cache. Spec line 107 deletes the files straight after the transaction, and line 13 sets the one-year immutable cache for /media. A browser holding the old catalogue JSON can therefore request a deleted file for up to about 60 s. The 404 is covered by the onError fallback on line 131, but the spec does not list this. The spec also does not say that browsers keep a removed photo for a year, which matters for a licence takedown. The fix does not reverse any owner decision, so it is not refuted. The severity stays minor.

findings.title: Storage service has no binary upload, content type, delete or policy code, and /media/ header handling is under-specified (x-amz-* cannot be hidden by wildcard; duplicate Cache-Control; cookies forwarded to MinIO)
findings.section: 1. Data and storage / 3. Serving and caching
findings.problem: ObjectStorage only has putText (hard-coded text/plain), getText and ensureBucket. The spec never says the WebP objects must be stored with ContentType image/webp, so MinIO would serve application/octet-stream, and with nosniff that breaks strict clients and the 'served file' checks. PutBucketPolicy replaces the whole bucket policy, and the spec does not say what happens if the MinIO key lacks permission or MinIO is down at start-up (ensureBucket's catch already creates a bucket on any error). In nginx, proxy_hide_header takes exact header names, so 'hides x-amz-*' cannot be written as a wildcard; MinIO's Server header, x-amz-request-id, x-amz-id-2, x-minio-* and any Cache-Control it sends (a second Cache-Control would sit beside add_header's) stay unless listed. proxy_pass with a URI keeps the Host default `host.docker.internal:9000`, which is correct for MinIO, but the browser's Cookie and Authorization headers are forwarded to MinIO.
findings.evidence: server/src/storage.service.ts:34-40 `putText ... ContentType: "text/plain; charset=utf-8"`; storage.service.ts:26-31 `try { HeadBucket } catch { CreateBucket }`; spec section 1: "At start-up the API sets a bucket policy that allows anonymous `s3:GetObject` on `media/*` only"; section 3: "hides MinIO's `x-amz-*` headers"
findings.fix:
Section 1, after the bucket policy bullet add: "`ObjectStorage` gains `putObject(key, buffer, contentType, cacheControl)`, `deleteObjects(keys)` and `ensurePublicMediaPolicy()`. Every WebP is stored with `ContentType: 'image/webp'`. The policy is exactly `{Version:'2012-10-17',Statement:[{Effect:'Allow',Principal:{AWS:['*']},Action:['s3:GetObject'],Resource:['arn:aws:s3:::${bucket}/media/*']}]}` and it replaces any existing bucket policy on the bucket. If the policy call fails, or MinIO is down at start-up, the API logs the error and keeps running, and the shop keeps serving. Image uploads and deletes answer 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE until the policy is applied. The policy is retried on the next start-up and before each upload."

Section 3, replace the "hides MinIO's `x-amz-*` headers" clause with: "`proxy_hide_header` is listed explicitly for each of Server, Cache-Control, x-amz-request-id, x-amz-id-2, x-amz-version-id, x-amz-server-side-encryption, x-minio-deployment-id, x-minio-error-code, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Xss-Protection, Content-Security-Policy and Vary, because nginx does not accept wildcards there. ETag and Content-Type are kept. nginx then adds its own single `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` with `always`. `/media/` also sets `proxy_set_header Cookie ''; proxy_set_header Authorization '';` so visitor credentials never reach MinIO."

Add to the dev checks: "`curl -sI <host>/media/<key>` returns `Content-Type: image/webp`, exactly one Cache-Control and no header starting with x-amz or x-minio."
findings.verifyReason: The spec grep has no ContentType or image/webp requirement for stored objects. Its only image/webp hit is the upload input's accept list on line 140. server/src/storage.service.ts has only putText, which hard-codes text/plain, plus getText and ensureBucket, and the spec never adds a binary put, a delete or a policy method. Without an explicit ContentType, MinIO would serve application/octet-stream. Line 57 says nothing about a failed or denied policy call. Line 116 says it "hides MinIO's x-amz-* headers", but proxy_hide_header takes exact names, so that cannot be written as a wildcard. MinIO's own Cache-Control would also sit beside the one nginx adds. nginx forwards the browser's Cookie and Authorization headers to the proxied MinIO by default. None of this reverses an owner decision, and the severity is minor.

findings.title: Product-page LCP is not met by eager + fetchpriority alone: the image URL is only known after JS and the catalogue API return, and thumbnails compete with it
findings.problem: The spec's performance goal is 'no layout shift', yet it adds eager and fetchpriority=high as the LCP measure. The site is a client-rendered SPA whose product data arrives through /v1/... after the JS bundle loads, so the browser cannot discover the photo earlier (no preload possible); the request chain is HTML, JS, catalogue JSON, image. On a 375 px phone, the up to six 48 px thumbnails sit in the first viewport right under the main photo; with loading=lazy they are fetched immediately and take bandwidth from the main photo on slow Indonesian mobile networks. No LCP target or check is given, so it is untestable.
findings.evidence: spec section 3 sizes table: "Product page main photo | ... | eager, `fetchpriority=\"high\"`"; "Product page thumbnails ... | lazy"; Testing lists no LCP or timing check
findings.fix: In section 3, after the sizes table, add: "The storefront is client-rendered, so the main photo URL is known only after the catalogue response (HTML, JS, catalogue JSON, image); no preload or SSR is added in this round. `fetchpriority="high"` on the main photo is the LCP measure. Product-page thumbnails use `loading="lazy"` and `fetchpriority="low"`, and their `` tags are rendered only after the main photo's `onLoad` or `onError` fires, so they never compete with it. Rows in carts, accounts and cards are unchanged." In Testing under "On dev", add: "Product page on a cold cache with Chrome DevTools 'Slow 4G' throttling at 390 px: the main photo is the LCP element and the thumbnail requests start after it finishes. Record the measured LCP in the dev checks; 2.5 s is the target to report against, not a release gate."
findings.verifyReason: The spec (section 3, lines 119-125) sets only eager + fetchpriority="high" for the main photo and lazy for thumbnails. Lazy images already inside the viewport are fetched immediately, and the up-to-6 thumbnails sit right under the main photo on a 375 px phone, so they compete with it. The spec says nothing about client-rendered discovery or load order, and its Testing section has no LCP or timing check, so the performance goal cannot be tested. This does not reverse any approved Item 1 decision, since only loading hints are involved. Two limits on the reviewer's fix: the thumbnails use the 480 px copy, so contention is modest, and a hard 2.5 s gate is a new number that the owner has not approved. Record the value instead of gating on it.

findings.title: Gallery: thumbnails' pressed state, variant sync and live changes are under-specified for screen readers
findings.problem: Variant selection changes the main photo and pressed thumbnail silently; the main img has no announcement that its content changed. Thumbnails sit as a bare row of buttons with no group name, and focus order relative to the variant fieldset (thumbnails in the left column, variants in the right column) is not stated, though reading order places 6 extra tab stops before the title. When the image fails to load (onError) the thumbnail row still shows broken/blank images.
findings.evidence: Spec: 'Picking a variant with a linked photo switches the main photo and presses its thumbnail' with no group role, name or live behavior; ProductPage.tsx:54-56 gallery column precedes the variant `<fieldset>` in DOM order.
findings.fix:
In section 4, product page gallery bullet, after "it has a visible focus ring." add: "The thumbnail row is `
`. The main `` alt always equals the alt of the selected photo, so it updates when a thumbnail or a variant changes the selection; no live region is added, because `aria-pressed` on the thumbnails already reports the change. Tab order follows the DOM: main photo, thumbnail row, then product details. A thumbnail whose image fails to load shows the `ProductArt` drawing like every other `ProductPhoto`, and the `aria-label` numbering does not change."
findings.verifyReason: The finding is only partly right. The spec (line 132) already gives each thumbnail an aria-label ("Foto 2 dari 4: {alt}"), aria-pressed and a visible focus ring. Line 131 says ProductPhoto falls back to ProductArt on onError, so a failed thumbnail shows the drawing, not a broken image. Two parts hold. The thumbnail row has no group role or name. Line 132 also says nothing about how the main photo's alt text changes. The tab-order point is weak. Thumbnails sit under the main photo in the same column, and DOM order already governs tab order (ProductPage.tsx:55 gallery, :68 variant fieldset). Hiding failed thumbnails and recomputing the count would conflict with the ProductPhoto fallback, so that part should be dropped. A live region is not needed because aria-pressed reports the thumbnail change. I did not check how screen readers behave on a variant-driven switch.

findings.title: Upload progress, drag-and-drop feedback and disabled state are incomplete
findings.problem: 'Mengunggah…' and a disabled button are specified, but not whether the text is announced, how the drop zone is operated without a pointer (the real input covers keyboard), whether a drop of several files or a non-image is rejected, or what happens to the typed alt text on failure. At six photos the upload area should be disabled with an explanation instead of failing with 409 after upload. A disabled button with `disabled` drops focus. The client also cannot know a 10 MB/480 px failure until after the transfer on slow Indonesian mobile networks, with no progress or cancel.
findings.evidence: Spec: '"Mengunggah…" and a disabled button while uploading' and 'Seventh photo | 409 | LIMIT_REACHED'.
findings.fix: In section 4, Admin, "Upload area" bullet, append: "Operation without a pointer: the drop zone is a convenience only; the real file input and the "Pilih file" button cover keyboard and touch. While uploading, the text "Mengunggah…" is in a `role="status"` region (`aria-live="polite"`), and the "Pilih file" button uses `aria-disabled="true"` (not the `disabled` attribute) so keyboard focus stays on it; its click and the drop handler do nothing while uploading. A drop accepts one image file only. If the drop holds more than one file, none is sent and the message "Unggah satu foto per kali." appears. The client pre-checks type (JPEG, PNG or WebP by MIME type or extension) and size (10 MB) before sending, and shows the same Bahasa messages as the server table ("Format tidak didukung. Gunakan JPG, PNG, atau WebP." and "Ukuran file maksimal 10 MB."). The 480 px minimum and the 40 megapixel limit are checked only by the server. The server remains the authority for every rule. When the product already has 6 photos, the upload area is replaced by the text "Sudah 6 foto. Hapus satu untuk menambah." and shows again after a deletion. The 409 `LIMIT_REACHED` stays as the server-side guard for races. After a failed upload the alt text field and the chosen file are kept, and the error appears under the upload area with `role="alert"`, so the staff member can fix the problem and retry without retyping. Progress bar and cancel are out of scope for this round."
findings.verifyReason: Spec line 140 only says "Mengunggah…" and a disabled button. It does not say how the status is announced, what happens when several files or a non-image are dropped, or what happens to the alt text after a failed upload. Line 144 has role="alert" only for errors. Line 167 shows the 6-photo limit surfacing as a 409 after the upload, and the "3/6 foto" count on line 138 means the client already knows when it is full. A native disabled button drops focus, which is a real a11y issue. The fix does not reverse any approved Item 1 decision. Two refinements: the client cannot check the 480 px minimum without decoding the image, so the pre-check covers type and size only and leaves 480 px and 40 MP to the server. Progress and cancel stay out of scope because the handoff does not decide them and they would add scope.

findings.title: Success criteria are not checkable as written: layout shift, 'every demo product', 'one-year immutable', audit coverage and the seed/remove scripts
findings.problem: 'No layout shift' has no metric or threshold; 'Every demo product shows real photos' contradicts 'A product without a safe photo keeps its drawing' and depends on the Appendix A list, so there is no pass condition; 'Every change is in the audit log' is checked in the tests for 5 codes but with no assertion that failed or rejected attempts write nothing and that VARIANT_IMAGE_LINKED records before/after imageId. The seed tests ('idempotent, skips products that already have photos, remove-samples touches only source: sample rows') need fake storage and a samples.json reader that are not specified (the same storage seam), and media:seed needs a failure mode (a missing file referenced in samples.json, a hash mismatch between committed WebP and recorded hash). 'sign-in check 12/12' etc. are existing checks with no stated count for the new Playwright run.
findings.evidence: Spec Goals: 'with no layout shift and a one-year immutable cache.' and 'Every demo product shows real photos ... A product without a safe photo keeps its drawing.' Testing seed bullet: 'Seed: idempotent, skips products that already have photos, and remove-samples touches only source: "sample" rows.'
findings.fix:
1. In "Goals and success criteria", replace "with no layout shift and a one-year immutable cache" with: "with a Cumulative Layout Shift of 0.00 on a category page and a product page at 390 px (Playwright PerformanceObserver 'layout-shift' entries; every img has width and height before it loads) and a one-year immutable cache (checked with curl -I on /media/...)."

2. In "Goals and success criteria", replace the sentence "Every demo product shows real photos on product cards, the product page, the cart and the account lists." with: "Every product listed as approved in Appendix A shows its photos on product cards, the product page, the cart and the account lists; every product not listed shows its drawing. `npm run media:seed` prints the counts (added, skipped) and exits non-zero if samples.json references a file that does not exist or if the recorded hash does not match the committed WebP."

3. In Section 2, after "Order of work", add: "Storage sits behind a small `ObjectStorage` interface (put, delete, exists) in `server/src/media/`, with a MinIO implementation and an in-memory fake for tests. This seam is new in this round."

4. In Testing, replace "One audit entry per change with before and after." with: "One audit entry per successful change, with before and after. A rejected request (403, 409, 415, 413, 422, 503) writes no audit entry and leaves no database rows and no files in storage. VARIANT_IMAGE_LINKED records before and after imageId, and null is allowed for either." Replace the Seed bullet with: "Seed (run against the in-memory ObjectStorage fake and the fake database): idempotent when run twice; skips products that already have photos, including after a staff upload on one product; fails with a non-zero exit and writes nothing when samples.json references a missing file or a recorded hash does not match its file; `remove-samples` deletes only `source: \"sample\"` rows and files, writes audit entries, and leaves staff uploads untouched."

5. In "On dev, after deploy", change the Playwright bullet to also state the expected count: "Playwright new checks: product page photo loaded (naturalWidth > 0), thumbnail switching, variant switching, Marketing uploads a photo, Operations has no 'Produk' item and gets 403 from the API, CLS 0.00 at 390 px; all must pass (the run prints N/N)."
findings.verifyReason: Checked the spec text and the Item 1 decisions in the handoff. The fix reverses none of them. Four of the gaps are real. (1) Goals line 13 says "no layout shift" with no metric, and the Testing section has no CLS check. (2) Goals line 11 says "Every demo product shows real photos" and also "A product without a safe photo keeps its drawing", and Appendix A is empty and pending, so the first claim has no pass condition. (3) Seed behaviour in Section 5 and Testing line 189 gives no failure mode for a missing file or a hash mismatch against samples.json. The spec never defines a storage seam or fake either, only the existing `src/test/fake-db.ts` (Testing line 185); the tests need an object-storage fake and a samples.json reader, and neither is specified. (4) Testing line 187 says "One audit entry per change with before and after" but is silent on rejected requests writing nothing and on whether VARIANT_IMAGE_LINKED records a null imageId. The upload ordering in Section 2 (files first, then one transaction, files deleted if it fails) implies the no-leftover behaviour, but no test asserts it. I could not confirm the sign-in count point; the 12/12 checks are existing checks and the new Playwright run has no stated count, which is cosmetic. Severity stays minor. Two corrections to the reviewer's fix: the "in-memory ObjectStorage fake" is not an existing seam, so the spec must introduce it, and the CLS threshold should be expressed against the existing 390 px screenshot step.

findings.title: Alt text for sample photos is accurate-by-assumption: no rule against describing a photo as the actual product
findings.problem: The default alt text is 'Foto {nama produk}' (and the example 'Foto kabel USB-C hitam 2 m' is a specific product claim). For a sample photo of a similar item, alt text that states colour or length asserts product facts that may not match the variant being sold, which also feeds the consumer-protection risk above and screen reader users.
findings.evidence: Spec line 65: `"alt": "Foto kabel USB-C hitam 2 m"`; line 94: 'The admin form prefills "Foto {nama produk}"'.
findings.fix:
1. Add to section 5 (Demo photos), after the line about samples.json:
"Sample alt text (the `alt` field in `samples.json`) describes only what is visible: object type, colour and setting. It starts with \"Foto contoh: \" and never states length, capacity, volume, model, material or other specifications, because the sample may not match the variant being sold. Appendix A lists the proposed alt text next to each candidate photo, and the owner approves it with the photo. Staff uploads keep the prefill \"Foto {nama produk}\", and staff may edit it."

2. Replace the example on line 63 `"alt": "Foto kabel USB-C hitam 2 m"` with `"alt": "Foto contoh: kabel USB-C hitam melingkar di atas meja"`.

3. In the storefront gallery text (line 132), change the aria-label to `aria-label="Foto {n} dari {total}: {alt}"` and add: "When alt already starts with \"Foto contoh:\", the label drops the leading \"Foto\" from the pattern, so it reads \"Foto 2 dari 4: contoh: ...\" is avoided and instead reads \"Foto 2 dari 4, contoh: ...\"." Simpler alternative: keep the pattern as is and accept the duplicate word, noting it in the spec. In both cases, add the unit test "alt of a sample photo starts with 'Foto contoh:' and contains no digits followed by cm, m, ml, g, GB or W" to the seed-validation tests (section 7, tests)."
findings.verifyReason: The problem is real but minor. Spec line 63 uses the example alt "Foto kabel USB-C hitam 2 m", which states colour and length. Nothing in the spec limits what alt text on sample photos may claim. Line 94 prefills "Foto {nama produk}" for every photo, including samples. The spec already marks samples with a visible "Foto contoh" tag (line 143) and a banner. The alt text is the one place that marking is missing, and screen reader users get none of it. The fix applies only to seed sample photos and does not touch the approved default for staff uploads, so it does not reverse any Item 1 decision. Two refinements are needed. Line 63 should be changed, because it is the example that shows the problem. The aria-label on line 132 already starts with "Foto N dari M:", so a "Foto contoh:" prefix would read "Foto 2 dari 4: Foto contoh: ..." and needs a wording tweak.

The spec says 'a new "Before launch" item in docs/07-delivery/LAUNCH_CHECKLIST.md', which implies the file exists, but it does not. findings.title: Seed and concurrency tests assume database behaviour the fake DB does not have
findings.problem: The tests for 'two simultaneous uploads' and 'duplicate photo' depend on unique-key violations (P2002) on (productId, position) and (productId, hash). The existing fake-db.ts has no unique-constraint handling (no match for 'unique' or 'P2002'), so these tests would pass or fail by construction of the fake rather than by the real schema. The testing list also has no test for the nginx /media/ config, the bucket-policy startup call, or the storage failure (503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE) path, though the error table and risks depend on them.
findings.evidence: spec Testing: 'two simultaneous uploads (fake database like `src/test/fake-db.ts`)'; server/src/test/fake-db.ts: no 'unique' or 'P2002'
findings.fix:
In Testing, server unit tests, replace "two simultaneous uploads (fake database like `src/test/fake-db.ts`)" with: "two simultaneous uploads and duplicate photo, using a new media fake database built on the pattern of `src/test/fake-db.ts` (serialised transactions, rollback on throw) with a `productImage` model that throws Prisma P2002 with `meta.target` for each of the two unique keys `(productId, position)` and `(productId, hash)`; one test per key (position race retries or reports the conflict; duplicate hash returns the 'Foto ini sudah ada di produk ini' error). The fake only proves the service maps P2002 correctly; the real unique indexes are exercised by the dev checks below."

Add to server unit tests: "- Storage failure: a MinIO put failure returns 503 `STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE` and leaves no `ProductImage` row. - A failed transaction after upload removes the uploaded files only when no other row of that product uses the same hash. - The bucket policy built at start-up is JSON that allows only `s3:GetObject` for `Principal: *` on `arn:aws:s3:::${MINIO_BUCKET}/media/*`, with no `s3:ListBucket` and no other prefix."

Add to the dev checks: "- Upload the same JPEG twice to one product, and fire two uploads at once to one product: the second request is refused or retried, and the database holds exactly one row per `(productId, position)` and per `(productId, hash)`. - `GET /media/../health/x` and `GET /media/%2e%2e/health/x` answer 404 (nothing outside `media/` is reachable through nginx); `POST /media/...` is refused."
findings.verifyReason: server/src/test/fake-db.ts has no unique-constraint handling; its only unique-related code is a findUnique stub. It is also order-specific: it has no productImage model, so media tests need a new or extended fake either way. The Testing section (lines 177-200) lists a race test and a duplicate test but does not say the fake must emulate P2002 on the two unique keys. It also has no tests for the 503 STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE path (error table line 172), for the bucket policy call (line 57), or for orphan-file handling when a transaction fails. The dev checks cover listing 404s but not a path-traversal probe on the nginx /media/ location (lines 114-116). Impact is low and the fix reverses no owner decision, so it is minor but real. One caveat on the reviewer's wording: the fake only proves the service handles P2002 correctly. Real unique-index behaviour is proven by the dev checks, so add a dev-run check for it too.

findings.title: No performance budget or measurement for the catalogue payload, image bytes and processing time
findings.section: Goals and success criteria / 3. Serving and caching
findings.problem: The reason for the whole design is speed on Indonesian mobile networks, but no number is given. Each product now carries up to 6 images with a long srcset string and credit object in GET /v1/catalog, which is public, fetched on every page and refreshed every 15 s; with about 15 products that can add tens of KB of JSON to a response that previously was small. There is also no budget for page weight (bytes of images on a category page at 390 px), upload processing time, or the 1600 px copy, so 'resized WebP, no layout shift' cannot be accepted or rejected.
findings.evidence: spec lines 59-68 add `images` with full `srcset` to every product in GET /v1/catalog; success criteria lines 13 say only 'no layout shift and a one-year immutable cache'.
findings.fix:
Add to "Goals and success criteria", after the "Photos load as resized WebP..." bullet:

- Performance budgets, measured on dev after deploy and recorded with the other checks: (a) the gzipped `GET /v1/catalog` response for the demo catalogue grows by at most 15 KB compared with the response before this change; (b) a category page at 390 px loads at most 400 KB of image bytes before any scrolling (lazy images below the fold do not count); (c) the product page main photo is at most 150 KB at 390 px; (d) a 5 MB JPEG upload is processed (three WebP copies written and the row saved) in under 5 s on the dev VPS, and the API process memory does not grow by more than 300 MB during it. If budget (a) is exceeded, the catalogue may list only the main photo's `src`, `srcset`, `width`, `height` and `alt` per product (plus the linked photo of each variant), with the full `images` array and `credit` returned only by `GET /v1/products/:slug`. Do this only if cart, account and card views still show the right photo.

Add to "On dev, after deploy" (Testing section): "Measure budgets (a)-(d) above with curl --compressed, the browser network panel at 390 px, and a timed upload; record the numbers in the dev checks log."
findings.verifyReason: The gap is real. The goals (spec line 13) say only "no layout shift and a one-year immutable cache". Section 1 (lines 59-68) adds a full `images` array with `srcset` and an optional `credit` object to every product in the public `GET /v1/catalog`, which is refreshed every 15 s (line 118). Neither the success criteria nor the Testing section gives a number for catalogue size, image bytes on a category page, or upload processing time. The spec's stated reason for the design (speed on Indonesian mobile networks, approach A) therefore cannot be accepted or rejected by measurement. The size concern is modest: roughly 15 products x 6 images is about 30 KB raw JSON, which gzip (commit 4e13276) shrinks to a few KB. So "minor" is right. The reviewer's proposed shape change, main photo only in the catalogue, is not an approved owner decision, but it could break cart and account rows or variant photo switching if they read the catalogue. The fix should therefore set budgets and leave the response shape open as an implementation choice. The reviewer's fix does not reverse any item in "Item 1 decisions".

findings.title: Existing-data and fallback behaviour for deployed clients and for catalogue consumers is not stated
findings.problem: The spec does not say what happens to existing data and cached clients at the moment of deploy: the ProductImage table starts empty, the new fields are optional but the browser may hold a catalogue response (public, 15 s + 45 s stale) without them, and open carts or wishlists in localStorage hold product snapshots without images. It also does not say whether bootstrap.service (which seeds products on start) is affected, or whether product ids used in media paths ({productId}) are stable across a re-seed; a re-seed that regenerates ids would orphan every file and row.
findings.evidence: spec line 55: path uses `{productId}`; server/src/commerce/bootstrap.service.ts has its own onModuleInit seeding; spec line 70 only says 'the domain Product and Variant types ... gain the optional fields'.
findings.fix: Add to section 1, after the catalogue response description: "Existing data and deploy. No product, variant, order or cart row is changed except that `Variant` gains the nullable `imageId`. `ProductImage` starts empty. A product with no ProductImage rows returns `images: []` and the storefront shows the `ProductArt` drawing. Cart, wishlist and order data never store image data; the storefront reads photos from the live catalogue by product id, so a catalogue response cached before the deploy (up to 15 s fresh plus 45 s stale) simply lacks `images` and shows the drawing until it refreshes. `BootstrapService` and the catalogue seed are not changed: the seed upserts products by their fixed ids (B01, A01 ...) with an empty update, so ids used in `media/products/{productId}/` are stable across restarts and re-seeds. If a product row is ever deleted, its ProductImage rows go with it (Cascade) and its media files stay in the bucket as unlinked files; removing them is outside this change."
findings.verifyReason: The spec does not cover this: its only mentions are the optional fields (line 70) and the `{productId}` path (line 55). Part of the claim holds. bootstrap.service only calls catalog.reload(), auth.seedIfEmpty() and seedDummyExtras(). catalog.service seed() upserts products by fixed domain ids (`where: {id: p.id}`, `update: {}`), so ids are stable and a re-seed does not regenerate them. The 15 s catalogue cache and the empty ProductImage table at first deploy are real, but both are harmless because the fields are optional. Part of the claim is wrong. Grep finds no `localStorage` use in web/src, so the 'open carts in localStorage hold product snapshots' premise is unverified, and I did not check where the cart is stored. The Cascade-orphans-files point is real, but the fix cites a 'later cleanup job' that I did not confirm the spec defines. I did not check whether seedDummyExtras touches products. The finding is minor and its fix is a documentation clarification only.
